stories.title: Man kills girlfriend in hotel after she refuses sex:Took high-dose medicine in Firozabad; sister says friend got her killed
stories.summary: Kajal had my sister killed. She had her raped. Whenever these beasts appear before us, the pain will be unbearable. They should be hanged in front of us; only then will my sister get justice and we will find some peace. “Before leaving, she told me she was very hungry and asked me to cook something delicious for her. But she never made it home. My sister is gone, and I am left alone", said victim's sister. These words capture the grief of a family whose daughter was due to return home for Raksha Bandhan. Instead, her body arrived, leaving the family devastated. In Firozabad, on 26 August (Wednesday), a young woman was allegedly murdered by her lover after she refused to resume their relationship. The Dainik Bhaskar team travelled to the family’s home, around 30 km from the district headquarters, and spoke to her relatives about the incident. First, here’s what happened... A 21-year-old woman was allegedly murdered inside a hotel in Firozabad after refusing to have sex with her boyfriend for a second time. According to the police, the couple had sex earlier after the man took a sexual performance-enhancing drug. When he tried again late at night and she refused, he allegedly became enraged and slammed her head against a wall, killing her. Police disclosed details of the incident on Saturday, 29 August. The boyfriend lived 3 km from the girl’s home The woman was from a village under Nasirpur police station. Her family comprises her parents, an elder sister and two younger brothers. Her elder sister also works in a private job. The family’s financial condition is poor. Her father works as a farmer and labourer. The woman studied up to Class 12 at a school in another village, around 3 km from her home. The accused, Rahul alias Nitin, 24, also lived in the same village. Both studied together until Class 12 The girl and Rahul studied together until Class 12 and remained in contact afterwards. She later enrolled in a BSc in Biology and was in her third year. Alongside her degree, she was also pursuing a nursing certificate course in Firozabad. About two and a half months ago, she told her family that she and some of her college classmates had been sent to Gurugram for jobs. Started working at Blinkit without telling her family The girl travelled to Gurugram after informing her family. When her relatives made inquiries, they learnt that she had started working for Blinkit. The other students had also reportedly told their families the same story. Meanwhile, Rahul had started working at a dairy and in other related businesses in Shikohabad. Brother said, ‘My sister stopped me from coming to pick her up’ The girl’s younger brother said, “My sister had asked me to come home for Raksha Bandhan. She had left Gurugram by bus. We told her that I would come to Shikohabad to pick her up. “After reaching Shikohabad, she said there was a huge traffic jam and it had become quite late. She told me she would stay at her friend’s place instead.” Police answered when the family called The brother said, “I told my mother, and she spoke to my sister’s friend. The friend said there was no problem. She told my mother, ‘Auntie, she will stay with me tonight. We’ll send her home in the morning.’ “The next morning, something was being discussed in the village. We called my sister’s number, but the police answered. They told us that she had met with an accident and asked us to come to the police station. “When we reached the police station, they handed my sister’s body directly to us.” Couple had planned to meet on the girl’s birthday According to the police account, the girl had told her family that she would stay at her female friend’s house, but Rahul had already made plans to meet her. August 26 was the girl’s birthday, and the two had arranged to meet that evening. At around 8pm, she left her bag at her friend Kajal’s house and went with Rahul. 2 left for a hotel at 10pm Rahul met the girl at around 10pm. About 15 minutes later, they reached a hotel in Maiyama. According to police, Rahul had booked the room with the help of his friend Abhishek, whom he asked to remain outside. Inside the room, Rahul allegedly took a sexual performance-enhancing medicine before having sex with the girl. During the encounter, she began bleeding from her private parts, according to the police account. Boyfriend allegedly attacked her after she refused sex a second time At around 2.30am, Rahul allegedly tried to have sex with the girl again. When she refused, he became enraged and grabbed her by the head before repeatedly slamming it against a wall. She suffered a serious head injury and her condition deteriorated rapidly. She also sustained significant internal bleeding. As her condition worsened, Rahul and his friend Abhishek allegedly decided to take her to hospital on a motorcycle. Boyfriend rode the motorcycle as friend held her According to police, Rahul was riding the motorcycle with Abhishek seated behind him, while the girl was positioned between the two men. Police said her legs were bleeding during the journey and her clothes were stained with blood. At around 3am, they reached Maa Sawanti Devi Hospital beside the highway, where technician Hariom Yadav declared her dead. Police arrested Rahul, while Abhishek fled from the scene. Mother said, ‘She had been sent from the hostel’ Meanwhile, the girl’s family had been told by her friend Kajal that she would reach home by 8am. Her mother, speaking through tears, said, “My daughter had been sent out of Dev College’s hostel. Around 20 girls had gone together. We were told that she was working at a factory.” ‘The factory had closed for the day, so she was returning home’ “There was a holiday at the factory, so my daughter was returning home. We were in constant contact with her. She told me, ‘Mum, I’m coming home. I’m very hungry, so please cook something quickly.’ “I told her, ‘Come home, dear. I’ll cook something for you.’ “A girl named Kajal had been repeatedly calling her for the past three days and asking her to come to her. Kajal called me between 8pm and 8.30pm and said, ‘Auntie, don’t worry. Your daughter is absolutely fine. I’ll send her home between 7am and 8am.’ “But my daughter never came home. It was Kajal who got my daughter killed.” ‘She was returning home after 3 months’ The girl’s elder sister said, “She was returning home after three months. My sister had reached Shikohabad safely from Gurugram. She then went to Kajal’s room. Kajal even called our mother and assured her that my sister would reach home by morning. “But my sister never came home. We firmly believe that Kajal conspired with other boys to have my sister raped and then killed. “I am completely alone now. My sister, who was like my twin, has been snatched away from us. The accused should be sentenced to death; only then will my sister get justice.” Rural SP Anuj Chaudhary said, Accused Rahul has been arrested, and a rape charge has also been added. The police are investigating the role of the absconding accused, Abhishek, as well as the involvement of the friend. The mobile phone and other evidence are also being examined as part of the investigation.

stories.title: ‘IPS laughed while watching torture on video call’:Meerut victims say, ‘Made to drink urine; never saw officer as brutal as Avinash Pandey’
stories.summary: They stripped me naked in a room behind the SP’s office. The SP (Rural) forced my legs apart and beat me between them with a stick. Later, SSP Avinash Pandey arrived and ordered, ‘Take him to the police station.’ I was beaten there throughout the night and forced to drink urine. These are the allegations of Meerut resident Ravi Gautam, who says he was subjected to 24 hours of torture by the police for participating in a protest over the Lalita murder case. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Gautam said, “Was it my fault that I took part in the protest? I was tortured as if I were a criminal.” Gautam is not the only person to make such allegations against IPS officer Avinash Pandey. Two others, Digvijay Bhati and Anil Pradhan, have also accused him of torture. Bhati alleges that while he was being beaten, the torture was being shown to Pandey over a video call. “We were screaming in pain, and he was laughing,” he claimed. Pradhan has made similar allegations. Following the allegations, Pandey was removed from Meerut on August 20 and attached to the Lucknow headquarters. The Saharanpur DIG is investigating the matter, while it has emerged that the alleged assault took place inside the SP’s office. The SOG in-charge has also been suspended. Now, the victims recount, one by one, what they say happened to them. ‘SSP threatened to make me a leader; 10 policemen then beat me’ Ravi Gautam, a lawyer by profession, is the leader of the Yuva Shakti Dal and lives in Noida. He had joined a protest in Meerut over the Lalita murder case. During the protest on 8 July, SSP Avinash Pandey allegedly began slapping protesters. Gautam was taken into a police van. He says the SSP later climbed into the vehicle and slapped him eight to 10 times. We asked him what happened after he was beaten inside the van. Gautam said, “After beating me in the van, the police took me to the SP’s office. Two other people were also made to sit in the vehicle. After some time, Captain Avinash Pandey arrived and sent a constable to call me inside. “As soon as I entered, he abused me and said, ‘I’ll make a leader out of you today.’ “He then told around 10 policemen present in the room to ‘knock the arrogance out of him’. They began beating me. Some slapped me, while others hit me with their elbows. They then struck me with batons around 100 times. “I collapsed on the floor and was in severe pain, particularly in my chest.” ‘They stripped me naked and beat me throughout the night’ Ravi says that about an hour later, he was called back inside. He alleges that SP (Rural) Abhijeet Kumar, CO Saumya Asthana, Civil Lines police station SHO Saurabh Shukla and other officers were present. “SP (Rural) Abhijeet Kumar slapped me eight to 10 times. While abusing me, he said, ‘You have been externed from Noida. This is Meerut, and I know how to deal with people who hold protests here.’ “I tried to explain that whenever I took part in a protest anywhere, I informed the police officers beforehand.” Ravi then described what he called the most horrifying part of the alleged assault. “They took me to a room at the back of the SP’s office and told me to take off my clothes. I thought they would beat me in my underwear, but they made me remove that too. “SP (Rural) Abhijeet Kumar then began beating me. They continued assaulting me while hurling casteist abuses. They forced me to spread my legs and began hitting me between them with a stick. “After some time, Captain Avinash Pandey arrived and said, ‘Now take him to the police station.’” Ravi says he was taken to the police station at around 11pm, where the alleged assault continued. “Several policemen, including SHO Saurabh Shukla and Uday Pratap Singh, grabbed me and began beating me. They threatened to stage an encounter and kill me. “They kept beating me and repeatedly threatened to kill me in an encounter. They said, ‘Today, I’ll turn you into a bodybuilder.’ “They also took me to the cybercrime room on the right-hand side of Civil Lines police station, where they beat me again.” Allegation, ‘They gave me urine when I asked for water’ Ravi said, “I was extremely thirsty. When I asked the policemen for water, they gave me a yellow-coloured liquid. I believed it was urine. When I asked for water again, they abused me and said, ‘We’ll bring Bisleri water for you right now.’ “They continued beating me throughout the night. The next morning, I was produced in court and sent to jail. I was not given a medical examination. It was only after I reached Muzaffarnagar Jail that I underwent a medical examination.” ‘We will continue the protest sit-in until action is taken’ Ravi Gautam has been staging a protest at Commissioner’s Park in Meerut since 20 August. He says, “I have never seen such a cruel officer.” He has put forward three demands: ‘He objected to the abusive language, which upset the SSP’ Digvijay Bhati is another person who has accused SSP Avinash Pandey of assault. When the Samajwadi Party leader first appeared before the media on August 21, he had a serious injury to one of his eyes. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Digvijay said, “We went to meet SSP Avinash Pandey at around 11.30am on August 19. A history sheet had been opened against our colleague, Mohit Jatav. “Since we had met Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on August 17, Captain Avinash Pandey told us, ‘You people have become very big leaders.’ “During the conversation, he abused Mohit. I objected to it and stopped him. I believe this was what angered the SSP.” Digvijay alleges that he and Mohit were then dragged into the SSP’s cabin. “They started beating both of us with their hands and feet, shoes and belts. I grabbed his leg, and he kicked me hard in the eye. My eye immediately began to swell. “He then called SOG in-charge Akhilesh Kumar Gaur, who also beat me. We were later taken to the SOG office, where I was hung upside down. Four to five policemen continued beating me. “Akhilesh was showing everything to Avinash Pandey over a video call. We were screaming in pain, and he was laughing.” Digvijay says that even in the Lalita Gautam case, an FIR was registered against him and he was sent to jail despite not being present at the protest site. “I was not there, and there is no photograph or video showing me at the protest. Despite this, I was harassed and jailed. I want action to be taken against Avinash Pandey. If no action is taken, I will immolate myself,” he said. ‘SSP is casteist, he would call me to his office and beat me’ Anil Pradhan has been practising law in Meerut for several years. He had also filed a complaint with the DIG against SSP Avinash Pandey. Our team spoke to Pradhan about his allegations. “Avinash is a casteist person. He is prejudiced against Dalits and Muslims. Whenever he felt like it, he would call me to his office and beat me. I had never had a dispute with any police officer before, but he started creating problems as soon as he arrived,” Anil alleged. He recalled an incident involving a cyber-fraud case. “We had a cyber-fraud case. After investigating it, the local police submitted their report. When we went to meet the SSP regarding the case, his representative told us that the investigation had been closed. “We asked how the investigation could be closed when an FIR had not even been registered. When the SSP came to know about this, he started speaking to us rudely. We told him that we were both lawyers and victims in the case.” ‘If you did not commit the crime, why were you sent to jail?’ Speaking about the Lalita Gautam murder case, Anil Pradhan said, “The police were continuously protecting the main accused, Ankit Kumar. Perhaps this was because he was in the PAC. “When we sat down to stage a protest, the police arrived and began slapping people. While abusing us, they said that we had dirtied the road. “On the same day, after pressure was brought to bear on the police, they arrested Ankit Kumar in connection with the murder under Section 302 of the IPC and sent him to jail.” IPS officer Avinash Pandey, ‘I will respond in court’ We spoke to IPS officer Avinash Pandey about the allegations. He said, “I have already said whatever I had to say about this matter. I have nothing more to add at this stage. I have also returned from Meerut. “Local officials are looking into the matter. Whatever needs to be addressed will be dealt with in court.” An investigation is underway into the alleged assault of Digvijay Bhati and Mohit Jatav. SOG in-charge Akhilesh Gaur has already been suspended. Protests against Avinash Pandey and in support of Digvijay Bhati are being held across areas from Meerut to Sambhal. A panchayat has also been called to discuss the matter. Officials have sought 15 days to take action.

stories.title: SHO found dead in govt quarters in Basti:Hanged himself in uniform; status read, ‘Money is not greater than love’
stories.summary: Walterganj police station in-charge Surya Prakash Singh allegedly died by suicide by hanging himself at around 6.30 pm on Saturday. His body was found at his government residence. As soon as the information was received, several police officers, including the ASP, reached the spot. The incident took place near the Collectorate in the Kotwali police station area. According to police, Surya Prakash Singh hanged himself from a fan using a gamcha. After receiving information about the incident, Kotwali police reached the spot. The scene of the incident is around 3.5 km from Kotwali police station. Made Walterganj police station in-charge on April 18 Surya Prakash Singh was originally from Bhilampur Chhapra village in the Ataraulia police station area of Azamgarh. He had been transferred to Basti from Siddharthnagar. After being posted at the police lines, he was made in charge of the Walterganj police station on April 18, 2026. At around 6:45 p.m., fellow sub-inspector Balram Gaur reached the government accommodation. The door was locked from inside. After breaking it open, he found Suryaprakash Singh hanging from the ceiling fan. Balram then informed senior police officials about the incident. The Additional SP and CO reached the spot soon after. The DIG said no suicide note was found at the scene. Teams from the police surveillance unit, forensic unit and field unit are examining the site and collecting evidence. A mobile phone was also recovered from the station house officer. Police are investigating the case scientifically, keeping all possible angles in mind.

stories.title: Man kills girlfriend by smashing her head against wall:Was having sex after taking medicine in Firozabad, got angry when she refused
stories.summary: Police have solved the mystery surrounding the suspicious death of a 21-year-old woman at a hotel in Firozabad, arresting her boyfriend, Rahul aka Nitin, in connection with the case. According to the investigation, Rahul allegedly took medication to enhance sexual performance and forcibly had sex with the woman before attacking her when she refused to have sex again around 2.30am. Police said, “Rahul allegedly slammed the woman’s head against a wall after she refused. Her condition deteriorated after she suffered a serious head injury. Rahul then allegedly took her to hospital on a motorcycle with his friend, where doctors declared her dead.” Rahul has been sent to jail, while police are searching for his friend. The incident took place in Shikohabad. Read the full case in sequence Called her to meet on the pretext of a birthday, took her to a hotel During police questioning, Rahul said that his birthday was on August 26. He used this as an excuse to call the young woman to meet him. The two already knew each other and had studied together up to Class 12. The 21-year-old woman was working for Blinkit in Gurugram after completing a BSc in Biology and a certificate course in nursing. On Raksha Bandhan, she was returning to her village, Nasirpur, from Gurugram. She left Gurugram at 12 noon and reached Shikohabad at around 8 p.m. She had also called home using her friend's phone. She told her family that it was already night and that she was not feeling well. She left her bag at her friend's house. After that, she left with Rahul. Rahul met her at 10 p.m. About 15 minutes later, they both reached a hotel in Maiyamai. Rahul had already booked a room with the help of his friend Abhishek. Rahul had asked Abhishek to stay outside. Forcibly had intercourse after taking medicine According to the police, Rahul took a sex-enhancing drug in the hotel room. He then forcibly had intercourse with the young woman. During this, she began bleeding from her private parts. At around 2:30 a.m., Rahul tried to force himself on her again. The young woman resisted. Enraged by her resistance, Rahul grabbed her head and slammed it against the wall. After she sustained a serious head injury, her condition deteriorated. She also suffered heavy internal bleeding. Based on the complaint filed by the family, police have added charges related to rape following the murder. Took her to the hospital seated between them on the bike When the young woman's condition deteriorated, Rahul and his friend Abhishek began taking her to the hospital on a motorcycle. Rahul was riding the motorcycle, while Abhishek was seated behind him. The young woman was seated between the two. According to the police, blood was flowing from the young woman's legs along the way. Her clothes were also stained with blood. At around 3 a.m., they reached Maa Sawanti Devi Hospital, located along the highway. After examining the young woman, hospital technician Hariom Yadav declared her dead. Police officers patrolling at night had spotted Rahul and Abhishek arriving on the motorcycle. Fearing that something untoward had happened, the police followed them to the hospital. When the two men reached the hospital with the young woman, the police also arrived shortly afterward. As soon as he saw the police, Abhishek fled the spot, while Rahul was arrested. She was returning home from Gurugram for Raksha Bandhan The deceased was a resident of a village in the Nasirpur area. According to the family, they had expected their daughter to come home for the festival, but the next day they received news of her death. They accused Rahul and others of murder and demanded the arrest of the accused. Protest lasted for several hours with the body, demand for hanging After the young woman's death, her family members and villagers became enraged. They placed her body on the Shikohabad-Nasirpur road and staged a protest. During the protest, which continued for several hours, people demanded the arrest of the accused and strict action against them. The family members said that the young woman had been wronged and that those responsible for her death should face stringent punishment. The police persuaded the protesters to end the demonstration by assuring them of action. The arrival of the village girl's body just before the Raksha Bandhan festival plunged the entire family into mourning. Cries of grief echoed through the house where preparations for the festival were supposed to be underway. Rape charge added after murder case was registered On August 27, a case was registered at the Shikohabad police station under charges of murder and the SC/ST Act based on a complaint filed by the young woman's father. According to the police, the post-mortem report, questioning, and evidence collected indicated that the young woman had been subjected to forced sexual intercourse. Following this, Section 64(1) of the BNS, pertaining to rape, was added to the case. The post-mortem report stated that a serious head injury was the cause of death. Young Woman's Mobile Phone and Sexual Performance-Enhancing Medication Recovered Police recovered the young woman's blue Vivo mobile phone from Rahul. In addition, a black Samsung mobile phone and a strip of a sexual-performance-enhancing medication named VIGORE 100 GERMED were also found. According to police, two of the four tablets in the strip remained, while two had been used. Police have included the mobile phones and medication in the investigation. Friend Absconding; Police Also Investigating the Female Friend's Role Abhishek's name emerged during police questioning. According to the police, he helped Rahul obtain a room at the hotel and was present outside during the incident. He was also with Rahul while taking the young woman to the hospital, but fled after seeing the police. Police teams are conducting raids to arrest Abhishek. Meanwhile, the role of the female friend at whose house the young woman had left her bag is also being investigated. The police are trying to determine the circumstances under which the young woman reached the hotel with Rahul and who was in contact with her before and after the incident. Police said-further action will be based on the evidence According to Rural Superintendent of Police Anuj Chaudhary, Rahul's involvement in the young woman's death has emerged based on the post-mortem report, police questioning, and the evidence collected so far. A charge under the rape law has also been added against him. The police are now investigating the arrest of absconding Abhishek, the role of the friend, and other evidence, including mobile phone records. Officials said that further action would be taken based on the facts that emerge during the investigation.

stories.title: Man who raped and killed 6-year-old girl killed in encounter:Dumped body in sack in Noida; police gunned him down within 24 hours
stories.summary: The accused in the rape and murder of a six-year-old girl in Greater Noida was killed in a police encounter. At around 5 pm on Saturday, police took the accused to recover the girl's body. While returning after recovering the body, the accused allegedly tried to escape from police custody. Police opened fire during the incident, injuring him. He later died while undergoing treatment at a hospital. The six-year-old girl had gone missing from her home on August 28 (Friday). Following a complaint from her family, police registered a case and launched a search operation. Five teams were formed and investigators began examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area. Meanwhile, the girl's family caught Balraj and handed him over to police. He was living as a tenant at the girl's uncle's house. CCTV footage showed him carrying the girl in a sack. Police arrested Balraj on Saturday afternoon. The incident took place under the jurisdiction of the Ecotech-3 police station. See 2 pictures... Girl's body found in a sack in a field A man living in Haldouni village worked as a confectioner. He had one son and two daughters. His youngest daughter studied in Class 1 at a government school near their home. Balraj was living as a tenant at the girl's uncle's house and was well known to her family. Police questioned Balraj. Initially, he kept avoiding questions, but later allegedly confessed to the crime. Based on information provided by Balraj, police recovered the girl's body from inside a sack in a field around 2 km from the village. The family alleged that Balraj, being known to them, lured the girl away with him. They alleged that he sexually assaulted her and later killed her. Balraj is also said to be addicted to drugs. According to police, a panel of doctors conducted the post-mortem examination of the girl's body with videography. The post-mortem report is expected to establish the cause of the girl's death and reveal several important facts related to the incident. Two CCTV videos emerge CCTV footage from around 3 pm on Friday showed the girl going with her neighbour Balraj. She is seen entering a house with him. Police also recovered another CCTV recording in which Balraj is seen carrying a sack. The second CCTV footage was recorded at around 5 pm. Both CCTV cameras were located in the girl's lane. Uncle says, 'Our girl must get justice' The girl's uncle said, "My niece was very young. A man used to live here as a tenant and worked as a labourer. Sometimes, he would also sleep in our rooms. The same person took the girl away after putting her inside a sack. We saw him carrying the girl in the sack in the CCTV footage. There was no one at home when he took her away. The children had gone to offer namaz and I was also not at home. "After the incident, we searched for the girl throughout the village and also made announcements, but she could not be found. We then checked the CCTV footage, which revealed the entire incident. The accused, Balraj, has been caught and handed over to police. I appeal to the government and police with folded hands to ensure that our girl gets justice." Investigation underway from all angles, including rape Police officers and an FSL team have inspected the scene. Police are investigating the motive behind the girl's murder and the sequence of events. Evidence is being collected while considering all possible angles, including rape. DCP Shailendra Kumar Singh said, “The girl went missing on the night of August 28. As soon as the information was received, a case was registered under the relevant sections. ” He added, "Five police teams were then formed, and a search operation was launched to recover the girl. An intensive search was carried out using CCTV footage and other means. Police teams searched for the girl with the help of local residents. During the search, the girl's body was recovered nearby."

stories.title: Chandrachur Singh’s haveli allegedly seized, FIR against 7, including aunt:Brother alleges fake will used to grab property
stories.summary: Actor Chandrachur Singh’s brother, Abhimanyu Singh, filed an FIR against seven people, including his aunt, at Roravar police station in Aligarh on Friday (August 28), alleging that they had occupied family land worth crores of rupees and an ancestral mansion and prepared a forged will. Abhimanyu said, “After filing a case in civil court, we have now taken criminal action. The police will deal with it from here.” Speaking on Saturday (August 29), Abhimanyu said, “The family's lands are spread across Jalalpur and several surrounding villages. There is also an ancestral mansion known as Jalalpur Estate, which my aunt Gayatri Devi Singh has occupied in collusion with seven other people.” The FIR names Gayatri Devi Singh, Jai Singh, Anjani Singh, Robin Aakeson, Sandeep Kumar Singh, Shiv Kumar and Ajit Singh Tomar as accused. An unidentified person has also been named as an accused. Now read the full matter in detail... Actor Chandrachur Singh belongs to the Jalalpur Estate family Chandrachur Singh has worked in films such as Maachis, Josh, and Kya Kehna. His family is counted among Aligarh's old zamindar families. His father, Captain Baldev Singh, served as an officer in the Indian Army. He was elected MLA from the Sadar Assembly constituency in 1985. The family's lands are spread across Jalalpur and several surrounding villages. Small and large disputes over the land had occurred in the past as well, but this is the first time the matter has come out into the open. Dispute escalated after uncle's death Chandrachur's uncle, Ganga Singh, had been living in Sweden for a long time. After his brother's death, Ganga Singh came to live at the Jalalpur mansion. Ganga Singh died in October 2025. Since then, tensions within the family have intensified over possession of and claims to the ancestral property, the mansion, and land associated with the trust. Now read what Chandrachud's brother Abhimanyu revealed... Forged Will, prepared a day before Grandfather's death Our grandfather was a very prominent zamindar in Aligarh. He passed away in 1997. A forged will was prepared just one day before his death. Along with some family members, outsiders were also involved in this major conspiracy. Through this forged will, all the valuable land was transferred in the names of a single family and two individuals. Collusion with tehsil officials The will was never probated either. Uncle Ganga Singh's wife and son fraudulently took possession of the mansion and the land. In an extremely devious manner, they colluded with officials and employees of the tehsil office to manipulate the revenue records. By changing the names, they illegally sold these properties for years. We were in Mumbai while this was happening behind our backs My family had been living in Mumbai for a long time. Since we lived far from Aligarh, we had no inkling that our ancestral properties were being occupied and sold. Now that we have learnt about the fraud, we have engaged a legal team. The ancestral property also includes the historic mansion, The Jalalpur Estate, built in 1870. It is a heritage property. All the documents have been retrieved, and complaints have been submitted to senior officials. Case had reached court; criminal action will now follow Chandrachud's brother Abhimanyu said, "I had filed a civil suit in the Aligarh court. I had been continuously gathering evidence for the past two months. Now, I have had a criminal case registered in this matter." Not only family members are involved in this land dispute and fraud, but some local politicians are also trying to get involved in it through improper means. Legal action has been taken against all of them.

stories.title: Surgeons from across India to gather in Gorakhpur:AI and robotic surgery to be discussed; patients to benefit from advances
stories.summary: A major event in the field of medicine and surgery is set to take place in Gorakhpur. The national-level conference of the Uttar Pradesh Association of Surgeons of India (UPASI), UPASICON 2026, will be held in Gorakhpur this year. The four-day conference will be held at AIIMS Gorakhpur from November 26 to 29. On Saturday, UPASICON 2026 organising secretary Dr Shiv Shankar Shahi and organising chairman Dr Gaurav Gupta held a press conference and shared details about the event. They said that a large number of surgeons, specialist doctors, and representatives associated with the medical field from various districts of Uttar Pradesh as well as different parts of the country will attend the conference. Special Discussion on AI and Robotic Surgery At UPASICON 2026, experts will discuss new techniques in modern surgery and innovative treatment methods. Particular focus will be placed on the role of rapidly advancing technologies in the medical field, including artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and other modern innovations. Experts will also explain how these technologies can be used to make surgeries safer and more effective. Doctors from across the country will share their experiences and the latest insights at the conference. Hands-on Training to Be Held on November 26 Hands-on training will be organised on November 26, the first day of the conference. The objective is not only to inform doctors about new technologies but also to provide them with practical training in their use. The training will include new doctors, physicians studying surgery, and experienced doctors who do not have much familiarity with modern technologies. During the training, doctors will receive practical instruction in robotic surgery, the medical applications of AI, laser, endoscopic and laparoscopic techniques, as well as techniques such as radiofrequency ablation. Scientific sessions to be held from November 27 to 29 Separate scientific sessions will be organised on November 27, 28, and 29 as part of the conference. These sessions will discuss new research, modern technologies, and new treatment methods in the field of surgery. In addition, doctors' experiences and the challenges encountered during the treatment of complex surgical cases will also be shared. This will give surgeons across the country an opportunity to learn from one another and gain knowledge about new techniques. Using Modern Technology According to the organisers, the conference's primary objective is to make new technologies accessible for the treatment of ordinary patients. For this, it is essential that doctors continuously stay updated with modern knowledge and techniques. The proper use of new technologies can help provide patients with better, safer, simpler, and more affordable treatment. In particular, AI and robotics may play an important role in the field of surgery in the coming years. Modern Surgical Facilities Expanding in Gorakhpur It was also stated at the press conference that Gorakhpur is now progressing rapidly in the field of medicine. Several modern facilities have become available in the city, particularly in the field of surgery. Many of the complex surgeries that previously required patients to travel to Lucknow, Delhi, Mumbai, or other major cities are now available in Gorakhpur as well. In this context, UPASICON 2026 will be a major opportunity to showcase Gorakhpur's medical facilities and the capabilities of its specialist doctors to the entire country. Gorakhpur's Art and Culture Will Also Be Showcased Along with medicine, there are plans to showcase the art, culture, handicrafts, and local products of Gorakhpur and Purvanchal to doctors arriving from across the country at UPASICON 2026. The organisers have appealed to businesspeople, social workers, public representatives, officials, and other members of society in Gorakhpur to showcase local art and products through stalls or exhibitions at the conference venue. Gorakhpur is known for its terracotta, Gita Press, handicrafts, and various products prepared locally. Their display at the conference will give doctors coming from different parts of the country an opportunity to learn about Gorakhpur's culture and local talent. Conference Held in a Different City Every Year UPASI organises this scientific conference every year in different cities across Uttar Pradesh. Agra hosted it in 2024, Kanpur in 2025, and now Gorakhpur has been chosen to host this major event in 2026. The organisers say that medical science is changing rapidly. Therefore, it is essential for doctors to keep pace with new technologies. Only by understanding modern technologies and receiving proper training in their use can patients benefit from them safely and effectively. An Opportunity to Showcase Gorakhpur on the National Stage UPASICON 2026 in Gorakhpur is not just a medical conference. It is also an opportunity to showcase the city's modern medical facilities, specialist doctors, local art, culture, and talent at the national level. During this four-day conference, surgeons and specialist doctors from across the country will discuss the future of modern surgery, new technologies, and evolving treatment methods. It is also expected to further strengthen Gorakhpur's growing recognition in the medical field.

stories.title: Man clashes with traffic cop after being stopped on bike:They get into scuffle, tears uniform; 20-minute confrontation
stories.summary: In Mainpuri city on Saturday morning, a traffic police officer on duty faced severe consequences simply for stopping a motorcyclist. After the bike was pulled over, the motorist began verbally abusing the traffic constable. As the argument escalated, it led to physical violence. It is alleged that the youth assaulted the police officer. During the incident, the constable's uniform was torn, and he sustained injuries. A video of the incident is also going viral on social media. The police have taken the motorcyclist, his father, and his brother into custody in connection with the case. The incident occurred near the Atal police outpost located near the Exhibition Ground in the City Kotwali area. On Saturday morning, traffic constable Yajuvendra Kumar was deployed there on duty. During this time, a young motorcyclist was passing through the area. The police officer signalled the biker to stop, but he did not pull over. After moving a short distance forward, he stopped at a grocery shop. Following this, Constable Yajuvendra Kumar also arrived there from behind. It is reported that a heated argument broke out between the two over stopping the motorcycle. Within a short time, the dispute escalated to the point where physical violence broke out between them. It is alleged that the motorcyclist assaulted the police officer. During the altercation, the constable's uniform was torn, and he sustained injuries to his body. People present at the scene attempted to stop the duo, but the dispute did not settle quickly. The argument and physical fight continued at the spot for about 20 to 25 minutes. During this time, someone recorded a video of the entire incident on a mobile phone. Later, this video went viral on social media. After the video surfaced, activity intensified within the police department regarding the matter. According to available information, the motorcyclist has been identified as Piyush Yadav, son of Gajraj Yadav. During the dispute, Piyush also called his father, Gajraj Yadav, and brother, Vivek Yadav, to the scene. Upon receiving information about the incident, Civil Line Outpost In-charge Dinesh Kumar arrived at the spot with a police force.

stories.title: Woman constable dies, denied leave after accident:Husband breaks down in Basti; says she would be alive if treated
stories.summary: Woman constable in Uttar Pradesh’s Basti district, who was injured in a road accident seven days ago, died on Saturday. She had received four stitches to her head after the accident. The constable, Kesari Verma (30), had submitted a leave application at the SP’s office so she could seek medical treatment, but her leave was allegedly not granted. Kesari’s husband, Nagendra Verma, is also a police constable. After her death, he broke down outside the post-mortem house and alleged that the lack of timely treatment led to his wife’s death. He said she had been visiting the SP’s office for two days seeking leave, but was not granted it. Constable Nagendra Verma said: If my wife had been granted leave by the SP’s office and received treatment on time, she would be alive today. I had attached a copy of her CT scan with the leave application and clearly mentioned that she had four stitches on her head. Despite this, Deepak Mishra and another employee posted at the SP’s office did not grant her leave. They told her that neither earned leave nor medical leave would be approved. Strict action should be taken against both of them. Meanwhile, Rudhauli Circle Officer Anil Singh said, “The woman constable’s health suddenly deteriorated in the early hours of Saturday. She was taken to hospital, but she had already died by the time she arrived. The exact cause of death will be established through the post-mortem examination. The allegations made by her husband regarding the denial of leave are also being investigated.” Accident while returning by bike, suffered a head injury Originally from Pratapgarh, Kesari Verma was posted at Lalganj police station in Basti. Her husband, Nagendra, is also a constable at the same police station. Nagendra said Kesari had recently taken leave and gone to her home in Pratapgarh. After her leave ended on August 22, she was returning to Basti. Her brother was taking her to the railway station on a motorcycle when they met with an accident on the way. Kesari suffered a serious head injury. She received treatment in Pratapgarh, where doctors put four stitches in her head. After treatment, she returned to Basti, where she continued receiving medical care. She also resumed her duties. Husband says, ‘If no action is taken, we will die here’ Nagendra said Kesari needed leave to continue her treatment after suffering the head injury. On August 27, she went to the SP’s office to apply for leave. He said that had the authorities reviewed her medical documents and granted her leave, even for a few days, she could have received timely treatment. He alleged that no action had been taken against the police personnel who refused to grant her leave. “If no action is taken, we will perform her last rites here. We will die here. My wife lost her life because of their negligence. This is a case of murder,” he said. Health deteriorated suddenly on Saturday morning; died on the way to hospital At around 4am on Saturday, Kesari’s health suddenly deteriorated at home. As her condition became critical, her husband Nagendra and other police personnel rushed her to Kaili’s OPEC Hospital. However, she died on the way to the hospital. Husband seeks FIR against 2 police personnel Devastated by his wife’s death, Nagendra submitted a written complaint to Lalganj police station SHO Dinesh Chandra Chaudhary, seeking an FIR against two employees posted at the SP’s office. Police officers also spoke to Nagendra for a considerable time outside the post-mortem house regarding his demand. Harraiya Circle Officer Swarnima Singh, Rudhauli Circle Officer Anil Singh and other officials tried to calm him and assure him that his concerns would be looked into. Kesari was from the 2018 batch, husband is also a police constable Kesari Verma joined the police force as part of the 2018 batch. Around two years ago, she married Nagendra Verma, a constable from the 2020 batch. Nagendra is originally from Amethi. The couple currently lived in a rented house in Bankati town, under the Lalganj police station area of Basti district.

stories.title: SP leader lies in waterlogged street:Protests in Seer Govardhanpur, says officials ignored complaints
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Aman Yadav staged a unique protest by bathing in water accumulated on the road and lying down in the middle of the street in the Sir Govardhanpur area in Varanasi. He raised slogans against the administration and accused the municipal corporation of failing to address the problem despite repeated complaints. Yadav alleged that a temporary drainage arrangement was made on July 29 ahead of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s visit to the area. He claimed that the arrangement was removed and the drain was filled after the Chief Minister’s programme ended, causing wastewater to accumulate on the main road. According to Yadav, nearly a foot of drain water has remained stagnant on the road for around a month, causing inconvenience to local residents and commuters. He said local residents have repeatedly urged the authorities to drain the accumulated water. On several occasions, they pleaded with officials to install a generator and pump the water out, but no permanent solution was provided. Aman Yadav alleged that whenever a generator is brought to the site, the water is pumped out for only a short time. Officials then take photographs and videos and send them to the authorities before switching off the machine, he claimed. ‘A month has passed, but the assurances continue’ Aman Yadav said officials had repeatedly assured residents that the accumulated water would be drained sometimes within 10 minutes and sometimes within an hour but a month has now passed. He said the waterlogging is causing problems not only for local residents but also for elderly people, children and pedestrians using the route. Residents have also reported people slipping and falling because of the water and mud on the road. In a media statement issued before the protest, Yadav said residents of Sir Govardhanpur, frustrated by the prolonged waterlogging, were forced to bathe in the stagnant drain water as a form of protest. He described the demonstration as a symbolic protest against the poor drainage system in the area. Claim of complaints filed on municipal commissioner and CM portals According to Aman Yadav, a complaint about the waterlogging was submitted to the municipal commissioner. The issue was also brought to the attention of Pankaj Patel, the officer responsible for arrangements in the area. He further claimed that a complaint was filed through the Chief Minister’s public grievance portal. Despite complaints being made at multiple levels, he alleged that the problem remains unresolved. Yadav said the road connects Sant Ravidas Temple with Banaras Hindu University and is frequently used by senior officials, including the district magistrate and divisional commissioner. Despite this, he alleged that no action has been taken to address the prolonged waterlogging. Yadav demanded that the municipal corporation and district administration immediately drain the accumulated water and establish a permanent drainage system. He said authorities should repair the drainage network instead of relying on temporary generator-powered pumping, so that rainwater and sewage do not accumulate on the main road in the future.

stories.title: BJP leader stabbed to death in Bareilly:Surrounded and killed 500 meters from home; attackers had been lying in wait
stories.summary: BJP leader was stabbed to death by unidentified attackers while out for a walk after dinner in Bareilly on Friday night. The attackers, who were allegedly lying in wait about 500 metres from his home, intercepted him and stabbed him with a knife. He was rushed to a hospital in critical condition, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place around 10:30 p.m. in the Subhash Nagar police station area, about 2.5 km from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as 28-year-old Sachin Kashyap, divisional vice president of the BJP OBC Morcha. After hearing his cries for help, locals rushed to the spot, prompting the attackers to flee on a motorcycle. Based on a complaint filed by Kashyap’s family, police have registered a murder case against three unidentified people. A dispute over a financial transaction is emerging as a possible motive. See the pictures... Know the full story Sachin Kashyap (28) lived with his family in the Manjhe Wali Bagiya area of Bareilly and worked at a printing press. His brother Sunny said Sachin was married. The family includes their mother, Gudiya Devi, father, Chandra Prakash, two brothers and five sisters. Sachin’s wife and their three children, Mahima (12), Aruna (8) and Shivansh (4) also lived with them. Sachin was also the vice president of the BJP OBC Morcha in Maninath Mandal. After having dinner on Friday night, he went out for a walk at around 10 p.m. According to the family, some attackers were allegedly lying in wait about 500 metres from his home. As soon as they spotted Sachin, they intercepted him, abused him and attacked him with a knife. When people rushed to the spot after hearing the commotion, the attackers fled on a motorcycle. Locals informed Sachin’s family about the attack. When his relatives reached the spot, they found him unconscious and lying in a pool of blood. They informed the police and called an ambulance. Sachin was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. There had been a dispute over money According to Sachin’s brother, he had a financial dispute some time ago with a young man named Babu. The matter was later settled with the intervention of local residents and acquaintances. However, the family alleges that the other side continued to hold a grudge against Sachin and was responsible for his murder. The family has demanded strict action against the accused and called for them to be killed in an encounter, saying this would ensure justice for Sachin. Police say, ‘Accused will be arrested soon’ CO Nitin Kumar said, The accused have been identified. Several police teams are continuously conducting raids at their suspected hideouts to arrest them. They will be arrested soon.

stories.title: Yogi says Akhilesh should apologise to people:Built JPNIC for 'luxury' says jobs bonanza coming in UP
stories.summary: In Deoria, CM Yogi Adityanath announced that a “treasure trove of jobs” is about to open up in Uttar Pradesh. Preparations are underway to provide jobs to one lakh young people within a year, including the recruitment of 32,000 police personnel. An for the 13 lakh candidates who cleared the UP TET examination is also expected soon. Yogi also launched a scathing attack on Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, alleging that the SP “spent ₹862 crore like water” on the construction of the JPNIC. He claimed that a private limited company was formed in the name of JPNIC, involving Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav and their associates. Yogi said, These people used public money for their own indulgence. They should apologise to the people for this. With such a huge amount, schools, roads and industries could have been built for millions of people. CM Yogi visited Deoria on Saturday. Before addressing the public meeting, he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 80 projects worth ₹305 crore in Majhauliraj village for the Salempur and Bhatpar Rani assembly constituencies. The projects include the inauguration of 23 projects worth ₹139.47 crore and the foundation laying for 57 projects worth ₹165.50 crore. See the pictures... Now, read the key points from CM Yogi’s speech… 1- ‘SP means a gang of dacoits’ Targeting the SP, Yogi said, “SP means a gang of dacoits. Before 2017, there was a saying in the state: ‘See a Samajwadi, and the daughter is frightened.’ Every parent used to worry about their daughter’s safety. But that is no longer the situation.” Yogi said the media is the fourth pillar of democracy and highlights wrongdoing in the government and draws attention to its shortcomings. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav had once put a sword to a journalist’s throat. He also mocked Akhilesh, saying, “Babu used to wake up at 12 noon. His tutors would teach him afterward, but even then he could not understand anything. If you wake up at 12 noon, your head will remain heavy, and out of frustration, you will say anything.” 2- ‘Before 2017, there was neither security nor respect’ CM Yogi said that before 2017, there was a government and bureaucracy in the state, but neither security nor respect. He alleged that even basic facilities such as toilets were unavailable to the poor and that schools had become centres of cheating. The poor condition of schools, he said, reflected the poor state of governance. Referring to encephalitis, he said fear prevailed across Deoria and the entire Purvanchal region during the month of Sawan. Hundreds of people had died after contracting the disease, but the governments of the time failed to take adequate action. He alleged that no Chief Minister or Prime Minister from the SP or Congress governments came to the region to assess the situation. 3- ‘Another ₹150-200 crore will be needed for JPNIC’ Referring to the JP National Integration Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow, Yogi said another ₹150-200 crore would be required to complete the project. He said the BJP government came to power in 2017 and subsequently handed the project over to the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), which conducted an investigation. Yogi alleged that the SP spent ₹862 crore “like water” on the construction of JPNIC. He further alleged that a private company was formed in the name of JPNIC, involving Akhilesh Yadav, Dimple Yadav, Dharmendra Yadav and people close to the SP. He said, “These people used public money for their own indulgence. They should apologise to the people for this. With such a huge amount, schools, roads and industries could have been built for millions of people.” 4- ‘The mafia has been reduced to dust’ Yogi said disturbances used to occur before festivals under previous governments. He alleged that governments sold ration meant for the poor and provided protection to the mafia, which ran parallel administrations. “The situation has changed now. The mafia has been reduced to dust. Those who threatened the safety of daughters are either in jail or in hell,” he said. Yogi added that Uttar Pradesh was no longer in a situation of “one district, one mafia” and claimed that under the double-engine government, mothers no longer fear for their daughters’ safety. He also referred to the encephalitis outbreak in Deoria and the Purvanchal region, saying hundreds of people had died but the governments of the time failed to take adequate action. 3. ₹150-200 crore more needed for JPNIC Referring to the JP National Integration Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow, Yogi said another ₹150-200 crore would be required to complete the project. He said that after the BJP came to power in 2017, the project was handed over to the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA), which conducted an investigation that, according to him, brought the alleged irregularities in the project to light. 4. ‘Mafias have been reduced to dust’ Yogi said that disturbances were common before festivals under previous governments and alleged that the mafia enjoyed political protection. “The mafia has been wiped out,” he said, adding that those who threatened the safety of women are now either in jail or have met their end. He said the state is no longer dominated by “one district, one mafia” and claimed that under the double-engine government, parents no longer fear for their daughters’ safety. 5- ‘Poor getting ration, electricity and houses without asking’ Yogi said the poor are now receiving ration, electricity and housing without having to ask for them. Appointment letters are being issued to young people, and he claimed that the government has already handed appointment letters to 9.5 lakh youths. He said new enterprises are being established across the state, creating employment opportunities for local youth. 6- Mentioned free bus travel for women Yogi targeted the SP chief over the free bus travel facility provided to women on Raksha Bandhan. He said the facility was available to women from all communities, without any distinction between majority and minority groups. He claimed that 59 lakh women travelled free on July 27, while 60 lakh women availed themselves of the facility on Raksha Bandhan. 7- Praised former Congress MLA The Chief Minister praised former Congress MLA Raghav Baba for his stand during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. He said that despite the Congress government’s opposition to the movement, Raghav Baba had described Lord Ram as a symbol of honour, pride and glory and said opposition to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement in Ayodhya would not be acceptable. Yogi said Raghav Baba had opposed the Congress’s alleged appeasement politics during the movement. He said Deoria is now progressing, with a better connectivity network being developed across the district. Roads are being widened from four lanes to six and eight lanes in some areas, while schools are also being revamped. 8- ‘Preparing to provide jobs to 1 lakh youths within a year’ Yogi said the government is preparing to provide jobs to one lakh young people within a year. This includes the recruitment of 32,000 police personnel, 4,000 sub-inspectors and 45,000 Home Guards. He said the screening process for Home Guard recruitment is underway. He added that 13 lakh young people have cleared the UP TET examination and that the recruitment would be released soon. He said a “treasure trove” of employment and self-employment opportunities is set to open up for the state’s youth. 9- ‘Preparing to provide tablets to 2 crore youths’ Yogi said the government is preparing to distribute tablets to two crore young people, regardless of the subjects they are studying. Taking a swipe at the SP chief, he said, “This is what the SP chief is upset about.” He alleged that earlier, whenever government vacancies were announced, “the uncle and nephew” would set out with begging bowls, whereas young people in Deoria are now getting jobs.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at five-storey hospital in Bareilly:Wards fill with smoke, panic as families flee carrying children
stories.summary: Fire broke out on the top floor of the five-storey Navodaya Hospital in Bareilly on Saturday morning, sending thick smoke through the building and triggering panic among patients and their attendants. As the fire alarm sounded, relatives rushed patients out of the wards, while parents carried children in their arms and hospital staff evacuated critically ill patients on stretchers. The fire reportedly started around 10 a.m. in a room on the top floor, when the hospital was crowded due to OPD hours. Around 100 patients and attendants were present in the ICU and other wards at the time. Police and fire brigade teams reached the hospital soon after receiving the information and began rescue operations. The blaze was brought under control within around 30 minutes. The hospital administration arranged ambulances and shifted all patients to nearby hospitals as a precaution. The incident took place on Mini Bypass in the Izzatnagar police station area. A short circuit is suspected to have caused the fire. See pictures of the fire… Now, let’s understand the entire incident step by step 4-5 people trapped on upper floor, brought down through stairs Fire brigade employee Kapil Singh said 4-5 people were trapped on the upper floor. Heavy smoke made the rescue operation difficult. The team immediately reached the floor and safely brought everyone down through the staircase. He said the cause of the fire is being investigated. The hospital’s entry and exit routes, along with other fire-safety arrangements, are also being inspected. Patients shifted to nearby hospitals, staff monitoring them Hospital owner Umesh Gangwar said the top floor of the hospital has a rest room, where the fire broke out. The room had sofas and other furniture, which caused the fire to spread and generate thick smoke. The fire brigade arrived in time and brought the blaze under control, preventing it from spreading to other floors. However, the smoke triggered fire alarms on every floor. He said the hospital was evacuated as a precaution. The administration contacted nearby Raj Hospital and Prasap Hospital and shifted all patients there. Hospital staff were also moved to the nearby facilities and are monitoring the patients. Dr Umesh Gangwar said the top floor is generally not used and sees very little movement. The hospital has the necessary fire-safety arrangements in place. The canteen on the upper floor has also been closed for around one and a half years and has remained unused. So far, only one or two sofas are believed to have been damaged in the fire. No patient or other person was injured. Patients’ relatives worried outside the hospital Shahana, whose husband was admitted to the hospital: “My husband is undergoing treatment and was admitted to the general ward. I have just reached the hospital, so I don’t know where he is at the moment or which hospital he has been shifted to. I am trying to find out.” Haroon: “My father has been admitted to the hospital for the past 7-8 days. He had been suffering from a cough. I have just reached the hospital, so I don’t know what happened or how. I am trying to find out where my father is.” The news is being continuously updated....

stories.title: Singer Ankit’s wife breaks down, says, 'I’ll die by suicide':Demands encounter of husband’s killers, asks who will support family now
stories.summary: Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan’s wife Seema broke down in tears while appealing for justice after her husband was shot dead in broad daylight in Shamli on 26 August. Appearing before the media for the first time on Friday, she questioned how four armed assailants could carry out the killing in the heart of the city and escape despite police deployment across the area. Seema appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to ensure that the killers are arrested immediately or killed in an encounter. She also said that if justice is not delivered, she would take the extreme step of immolating herself along with her family. Meanwhile, police are examining newly surfaced CCTV footage to identify the shooters. The investigation has also been extended to suspected shooters linked to Panipat and Karnal, with the Haryana STF and Anti-Gangster Unit joining the probe. Singer Ankit Baliyan’s wife Seema shared these details... Iqra Hasan arranged a call between Akhilesh Yadav and Ankit’s family Earlier on Friday, Kairana MP Iqra Hasan visited Ankit Baliyan’s residence and met his father, Satyaveer Singh Fauji, and other family members to offer condolences. She said a memorial would be built in Ankit’s name using funds from the MP Local Area Development Scheme. Questioning the state’s law-and-order situation, Iqra said that if the case was not solved within four days, her party would stage a sit-in protest. She also arranged a phone call between Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Ankit’s family. Actor who claimed responsibility for murder seen celebrating Meanwhile, actor Bhupendra Dhingra, who had claimed responsibility for Ankit Baliyan’s murder, went live on social media again on Friday. In the livestream, he appeared to be laughing and celebrating, while some people were seen congratulating him. A young woman also appeared in the video and said that even if someone has a dispute with another person, they should not resort to killing. During the livestream, Dhingra appeared to say that a challan had been issued and a case registered at the police station, but that it took him only a short time to return to his old swagger and style. Three days ago, Dhingra, who describes himself as a singer and actor, had claimed responsibility for Ankit’s murder. He alleged that Ankit had misbehaved with him and hurled obscene abuses at him, and claimed that he killed him in retaliation. Dhingra is reportedly a native of Gurugram. Police have traced his current location to Karnataka. Investigators are also trying to establish whether he was actually involved in the murder or merely made a false claim of responsibility on social media. Sonipat criminal Bholu also claims responsibility for the murder Meanwhile, Sonipat resident Bholu Shahpuriya has also claimed responsibility for Ankit Baliyan’s murder. According to reports, several criminal cases have been registered against Bholu in Sonipat and other places. Identifying himself as a member of the Gogi Gang, he made a post on social media claiming responsibility for the killing. In the post, Bholu alleged that Ankit supported the gang’s rivals and had released a song about an incident involving gang member Gogi. He claimed that Ankit had backed their rivals in criminal activities and had therefore “faced the consequences.” He also issued a threat to others, saying that those who support their rivals would meet the same fate. What has police done so far in the murder case?

stories.title: Leopard kills 35-year-old man in Moradabad:Drags him from hut while he slept; 4 killed in 25 days
stories.summary: Leopard allegedly mauled a 35-year-old disabled man to death after dragging him from outside his home into a nearby forest in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The animal bit his neck and tore into his chest, leaving his blood-soaked body about 100 metres from the house. Jagraj was sleeping on a charpoy outside his home on Friday night when the leopard reportedly approached him, grabbed him by the neck and dragged him into the forest. When his family did not find him on the charpoy on Saturday morning, they began searching for him and later found his body in the forest. The incident took place in Bahapur Balia village under Thakurdwara police station. Three days earlier, a leopard had allegedly killed a woman working in a field in the same village. Four people have now died in leopard attacks in the area over the past 25 days. 3 pictures from the incident site… Jagraj put his children to sleep inside and slept outside the hut Divyang Jagraj (35) had built a hut-like house on the outskirts of Balia village. His wife died three years ago, after which he had been raising his 8-year-old son and 6-year-old daughter on his own. He supported the family by driving an e-rickshaw. Since the hut had no door, he would sleep outside. On Friday night, Jagraj fed his children and put them to sleep inside before lying down outside as usual. The leopard attacked and killed him while he was sleeping. After being informed, the Forest Department team reached the spot and began efforts to capture the animal. The department has installed trap cameras in the area and laid nets at several locations to monitor the leopard’s movements and capture it as soon as possible. DFO says, ‘No flooding this time, so farmers are spending more time in fields’ Moradabad Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Dr Vinay Kumar Pandey said the area is a natural habitat for leopards and such attacks have occurred in the past as well. He said that earlier, limited means of communication meant information about such incidents did not reach many people. This year, there has been no flooding, allowing farmers to regularly visit their fields. As a result, encounters between people and leopards have increased, which has also led to more reported attacks.

stories.title: ‘Have sex with me, I’ll get you educated in city’:College manager’s son raped student, threatened to fail her; FIR registered
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a Class 10 student has accused the son of a private school manager of rape. According to the girl, the accused sexually exploited her for four months and allegedly abused and threatened to fail her when she resisted. The accused allegedly told her, “If you want to progress and study in the city, have a relationship with me. I will bear all your expenses.” When she refused, he allegedly threatened to fail her if she did not sleep with him. He later allegedly made an audio recording of their conversation viral. After the audio surfaced, the student attempted suicide. The case is from the Gola police station area, around 55 km from the district headquarters. After learning about the girl’s ordeal, her younger sister informed the family. On Friday, the victim went to the police station with her grandfather. Based on her complaint, police registered a case against the accused under charges of rape and the POCSO Act. Calls her to cabin, threatens her and allegedly rapes her The 15 year old girl from Gola is a Class 10 student at a private girls’ inter college. She says her father works in Mumbai and alleges that Prateek Tripathi, the son of the college manager and a teacher there, had been harassing her. According to the student, around four months ago, Prateek called her to his cabin after classes. When she went there, he allegedly grabbed her and behaved inappropriately with her. When she resisted, he allegedly threatened to fail her if she did not have a physical relationship with him. He also allegedly threatened to defame her and assured her that no one would find out about their relationship. The girl alleges that Prateek raped her and took her phone number before contacting her regularly. He allegedly told her that he would help her progress, arrange for her to study in Gorakhpur city, get her a room and bear all her expenses. He also allegedly said he would speak to her grandfather. The girl alleges that he sexually assaulted her for four months. Distressed by the situation, she eventually told her younger sister, who counselled her. Now, know the full matter... A 15-year-old Class 10 student from the Gola area studies at a private girls’ inter college. According to the student, her father works in Mumbai, while she lives in the village with her mother, grandfather and younger sister. Prateek Tripathi, the school manager’s son, also teaches at the college. The student alleges that around four months ago, Prateek called her to his cabin after classes. He was alone in the cabin. She alleges that when she entered, he grabbed her and behaved inappropriately with her. When she resisted, he allegedly threatened to fail and defame her if she did not have a physical relationship with him. The accused allegedly told her that no one would find out about what happened between them. He then allegedly raped her. The student did not tell anyone about the incident at the time. She alleges that the accused took her mobile number and began contacting her over the phone. According to the student, the accused told her that he would help her progress, arrange for her to study in Gorakhpur city, get her a room and bear all her expenses. He also allegedly said that he would speak to her grandfather. The student alleges that he sexually exploited her for four months. Distressed by the situation, she eventually told her younger sister, who counselled her. Student refuses to meet him, accused allegedly makes audio viral The student said Prateek called her to meet him again one day, but she refused. Angry over this, he allegedly abused her over the phone and threatened to defame her. He allegedly told her that since he was bearing all her expenses, she should have no problem meeting him. The student still refused, following which he allegedly made an audio recording of their conversation viral. After learning that the audio had been circulated, the student attempted suicide. Since she had already told her younger sister about the alleged abuse, her sister counselled her. The student then told her family everything. Her family members were shocked after learning what had allegedly happened. On Friday, the girl’s grandfather took her to Gola police station, where she reported the entire matter. Based on her complaint, police registered an FIR against the school manager’s son. Her grandfather said the accused had repeatedly threatened to fail his granddaughter. He alleged that she suffered severe mental distress after the audio was circulated and attempted suicide. Meanwhile, after the audio surfaced, villagers reached the school, surrounded the accused and created a commotion. As the situation escalated, Prateek reportedly fled the village. He got married around one and a half years ago and has a two-and-a-half-month-old daughter. Both have been admitted to the hospital’s isolation ward and are currently in stable condition. Balrampur Hospital Director Dr B.K.S. Chauhan said RT-PCR tests confirmed H1N1 infection in both patients. They are receiving treatment under the supervision of senior physician Dr Anand. The isolation ward at Balrampur Hospital has been reserved for swine flu patients. With new cases being reported, the health department is closely monitoring the situation, while the government has directed all 75 districts in Uttar Pradesh to step up surveillance. DMs of all 75 districts directed to remain alert In view of the swine flu situation, the Yogi government has stepped up vigilance across Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed the Health Department and district magistrates of all 75 districts to maintain continuous monitoring. He has also asked officials to regularly review swine flu cases and ensure there is no negligence at any level. The Chief Minister has directed hospitals to maintain adequate treatment arrangements, including sufficient isolation wards, essential medicines, testing kits and other medical facilities, so that patients can receive immediate treatment when required. Travel history of infected patients to be checked Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said the number of patients reporting with fever has increased across the state, particularly in districts connected to the Delhi-NCR region. He has directed officials to check the travel history of all infected patients and advise them to undergo home isolation wherever necessary. He also instructed the Health Department to remain fully alert regarding swine flu. Get tested promptly if symptoms appear The Chief Minister has appealed to people across the state not to ignore symptoms of swine flu. Anyone developing symptoms should consult a doctor promptly and undergo the necessary tests. He said there is no need to panic, but timely testing and treatment are essential.

stories.title: CM Yogi orders strict action against land mafias and strongmen:Hears grievances of 200 people in Gorakhpur, assures justice for every victim
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath hears the grievances of around 200 people at a public grievance hearing at Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur on Saturday morning and directs officials to resolve their complaints promptly. People from several districts arrive with their grievances. The Chief Minister personally meets each complainant, listens to their concerns and accepts their written applications. He directs officials to take strict action against land mafias and influential individuals involved in illegal encroachments, while ensuring that every complaint is addressed sensitively and within the time frame. The Chief Minister says it is the government’s responsibility to ensure that every person receives justice without discrimination. Assures financial assistance for medical treatment Some people approached the public grievance hearing seeking financial assistance for the treatment of serious illnesses. The Chief Minister said, “No one’s treatment should be stopped because of a lack of money.” He directed officials to promptly prepare treatment cost estimates for needy patients so that government assistance could be provided without delay. The Chief Minister also took complaints related to revenue and law and order seriously and directed officials to resolve them promptly. In cases involving family disputes, he instructed officials to hear both sides and make efforts to resolve the issues amicably. Chief Minister performs cow service, feeds cattle jaggery and puri After the public hearing, the Chief Minister offered prayers and paid obeisance to Guru Gorakhnath at Gorakhnath Temple. He then paid his respects at the statue of his spiritual mentor, the late Mahant Avaidyanath, before touring the temple premises. The Chief Minister also visited the temple’s cowshed and performed cow service. He fed jaggery and puris to the cows with his own hands and inspected the arrangements at the cowshed.

stories.title: Bridge collapses in Moradabad, family swept away with bike:Mother dies, son missing, 3 rescued
stories.summary: Five members of a family riding a motorcycle fell into the Gagan River after a wooden bridge collapsed in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The woman died in the accident, while her young son remains missing. Villagers rescued her husband and two other children. The accident took place around 7:30 p.m. on Friday when the woman was returning from her parents’ home after tying a rakhi on her brother’s wrist for Raksha Bandhan. The family was crossing a small wooden bridge over the Gagan River at Chattha in Malkapur, under the Majhola police station area. As the motorcycle reached the bridge, some of the wooden planks suddenly broke. The motorcycle lost balance and plunged into the river along with the family. Hearing their cries for help, people nearby rushed to the spot and jumped into the river. The woman and one of her children were swept away by the strong current. Police launched a search for the mother and son with the help of local divers and an NDRF team. After around two hours, divers recovered the woman’s body. The child is still missing. Moradabad SSP Satpal Antil said teams are continuing the search for him. First, take a look at 3 pictures... Bike plunges into river, family cries out for help Labourer Anil Jatav (45), a resident of Mahmoodpur in Chhajlat, visits his in-laws’ home in Nanpur village of Kundarki on Raksha Bandhan with his wife Kiran (42), sons Keshav (7) and Priyanshu (3), and daughter Kafia (5). After the celebrations, the family begins their journey home on a motorcycle. As they reach the wooden plank bridge in Malkpur, three planks suddenly break. The motorcycle loses balance and plunges into the Gagan River along with the family. The family cries out for help. Hearing their cries, passers-by rush to the spot. Police also arrive with divers from Malkapur village. Anil, Keshav and Kafia are rescued, while Kiran dies. Priyanshu remains missing. Divers conduct search operation using flashlights According to the SSP, the rescue operation is difficult because it is already dark. Divers conduct the search using flashlights. Kiran is immediately taken to the district hospital, where doctors declare her dead. The search for the missing child resumes on Saturday morning, with an SDRF team also being called in to assist with the operation.
