stories.title: Ankit Baliyan murder case:2 Sonipat shooters killed in encounter; over 20 rounds fired, ₹50,000 reward on each
stories.summary: UP Police killed two shooters in an encounter in the Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan murder case. Police identified them as Sumit and Mohit, both residents of Sonipat. A ₹50,000 reward had been announced for each, and they were allegedly linked to the Gogi gang. Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said the two shooters were fleeing towards Sonipat on a motorcycle. Acting on a tip-off, police surrounded them on Monday morning. Fearing arrest, the suspects opened fire. Police retaliated, leading to around 20 rounds being fired from both sides. Sumit and Mohit were shot during the encounter. Police took them to hospital, where doctors declared them dead. The encounter took place in the Industrial police station area. According to police, the two men, along with two other accomplices, had allegedly shot dead Ankit outside a gym five days ago. The other two suspects, Satyam and Aryan, are still absconding. Meanwhile, after the encounter, the singer’s father, Satyaveer, told Dainik Bhaskar: “We have received half justice. Now we are fully hopeful that we will get complete justice. We had hope earlier too, but it was gradually fading. Shoot the others too; only then will we feel satisfied. Our trust in the police and Yogi ji has increased now. If no action had been taken today, our trust would have been broken. Half of the justice is still pending.” See the pictures related to the encounter… Ankit’s father says, ‘We have received only half justice; arrest other two accused too’ Ankit’s father, Satbir, told Dainik Bhaskar, “We have received half justice so far. Now we hope we will get complete justice. Earlier, our hope was gradually fading. The other two accused should also be dealt with; only then will we feel satisfied. Our trust in the police and Yogi ji has increased now. It has been 5–6 days. If no action had been taken today, our trust would have been broken. Half of the justice is still pending.” Read how the encounter unfolded… Barricading continued throughout the night after Ankit Baliyan’s murder Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said that after the murder of popular Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan, the SWAT team, surveillance unit, all SHOs, ASPs and COs of the city and Kairana were deployed to crack the case. Special barricading and vehicle checks were ordered across the district from midnight until 6 am to trace the accused. Suspects spotted at 4 am, opened fire at police when stopped According to the SP, suspects riding a motorcycle were spotted coming from the Karnal side at around 4 am. Police teams were immediately alerted. When SHO Dharmendra Gautam, who was checking vehicles at Madra bridge, tried to stop them, the suspects opened fire at the police, shattering the vehicle’s windscreen. Several police teams arrived after wireless alert Following the firing, police immediately issued an alert over the wireless network. The SWAT team, surveillance officer, SHO, ASP, CO City and CO Kairana then reached the spot. During the police cordon, the suspects changed the motorcycle’s route and tried to escape. Both suspects injured in retaliatory firing In the police response, Sumit and Mohit sustained serious gunshot injuries. Police took both of them to the hospital for treatment, where doctors declared them dead. According to police, both suspects suffered more than 20 gunshot wounds. After the encounter, police took control of the site and began an investigation. Weapons and other items recovered from the spot SP Narendra Pratap Singh said the two suspects killed in the encounter were involved in Ankit Baliyan’s murder. Police recovered weapons and other items from the scene. Investigators are now examining the recovered items and other evidence found at the site. Ankit was shot as soon as he came out of the gym. Here is the full case… In Shamli, attackers fired 18 rounds at 32-year-old YouTuber and Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan. He collapsed on the road after being hit by five bullets in the head and abdomen. Police took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Angry over the incident, local people blocked the road demanding the attackers’ arrest. Ankit’s mother sat on the road holding his body in her lap. ADG Meerut Zone Bhanu Bhaskar and DIG Saharanpur Range Abhishek Singh reached Shamli. The officers spoke to Ankit’s father and got the roadblock cleared. Just an hour before his murder, Ankit had posted a song on Instagram in which he was seen sitting in a car and singing, ‘Murder maar denge sadak ke upar’. Ankit often made songs about gun culture. His song ‘Bhari court mein goli marenge’ was released on 15 February 2023 and was later banned. He subsequently became well known in the Haryanvi music industry. Meanwhile, on Thursday, a gang calling itself the Haryana-based ‘Gogi Group’ claimed responsibility for the murder. A person from Sonipat named Bholu Shahpuriya, who is allegedly linked to the gang, shared a post on Instagram saying that Ankit supported their enemies and had made a song about an incident involving their ‘Gogi bhai’. He said Ankit had received the consequences. Later that evening, singer-actor Bhupendra Dhingra posted a video on his Instagram account claiming that he had a dispute with Ankit at the gym and had then called shooters to have him killed. Investigation reveals four shooters were involved in the murder The police investigation has revealed that four shooters carried out Ankit Baliyan’s murder. Of them, Sumit and Mohit were killed in the encounter. The two other alleged shooters, Satyam and Aryan, are now on the police’s radar. Following the deaths of Sumit and Mohit, police teams are searching for Satyam and Aryan. Separate teams are conducting raids at possible hideouts to arrest them. Police are also investigating the route the two suspects took after the murder and where they are currently hiding.

stories.title: Yamuna Expressway crash kills 4:Truck breaks divider, collides with car in opposite lane; bodies stuck to seats
stories.summary: A horrific accident occurred on the Yamuna Expressway in Jewar, Greater Noida, at around 11 p.m. on Sunday. A speeding truck went out of control, broke through the divider, and landed in the opposite lane. It then collided with a car coming from the opposite direction. Four people traveling in the car died on the spot. The accident took place in the Jewar police station area. The collision was so severe that the car was badly damaged. The bodies became stuck to the seats. As soon as they received the information, the Jewar police and rescue team reached the spot. The police cut open the doors to pull out the people trapped inside the damaged vehicles. First, take a look at the three pictures... Long traffic jam on the expressway Traffic came to a standstill on the Yamuna Expressway after the accident. Long queues of vehicles formed on both sides. The police and rescue teams began removing the damaged vehicles to restore traffic flow. Victims' identities not known Police have sent all four bodies for post-mortem examination. As of the time of writing, the deceased had not been identified. Police are working to establish their identities. The preliminary investigation suggests that the accident was caused by the truck going out of control. However, an investigation is underway to determine why the truck lost control.

stories.title: 4 Nishad Party MLAs put up BJP leaders’ photos:Sanjay Nishad angry, says 'ashamed to put party flag; will rethink tickets'
stories.summary: 4 MLAs of the Nishad Party have put up pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on their social media accounts. However, both the name and the flag of the Nishad Party are missing. The party's national president, Dr. Sanjay Nishad, says, "Some MLAs of my party feel ashamed to display their own flag and banner. They do not attend party meetings. We will have to think before giving tickets to such leaders again." The MLAs with whom Sanjay Nishad is upset include Anil Kumar Tripathi, MLA from the Mehdawal seat in Sant Kabir Nagar; Rishi Tripathi from the Nautanwa seat in Maharajganj; Vivekanand Pandey from the Khadda seat in Kushinagar; and Ramesh Singh from the Shahganj seat in Jaunpur. First, know how many total MLAs the Nishad Party has in UP In the 2022 UP Assembly elections, the Nishad Party was in an alliance with the BJP. It was allotted 16 seats. There was an agreement of two types regarding these: Now know those MLAs who are not promoting the Nishad Party Nishad Party MLA Anil Kumar Tripathi has been an active worker of the BJP. In the 2022 assembly elections, he was preparing to contest on a BJP ticket. However, the seat went to the Nishad Party's quota in the alliance. Following this, Anil Tripathi contested the election from the Nishad Party and won. His 4.5-year tenure as an MLA has been completed. Now, only the last 6 months remain. However, there is no mention of the Nishad Party in Anil Tripathi's Facebook page bio. The cover of his Facebook page features a picture of all the MLAs sitting in front of the Vidhan Sabha. MLA said - My car has flags of both parties MLA Anil Tripathi says - 'Nishad Party and BJP are alliance partners. My car has flags of both parties. I attend the programs and meetings of both the Nishad Party and the BJP. I actively participate in every program of Dr. Sanjay Nishad's son, Praveen Nishad. I have been the leader of the Nishad Party's legislative party for three years. This is the result of Dr. Sanjay Nishad's trust.' Before contesting the 2022 elections, MLA Rishi Tripathi was active in the BJP organization. He served as the district general secretary. Under the alliance, this seat went to the Nishad Party. Compelled by circumstances, Rishi Tripathi had to join the Nishad Party. Rishi Tripathi has a picture with Home Minister Amit Shah as his Facebook profile cover. A BJP flag is often seen on his vehicle. He is also frequently spotted at BJP meetings. In fact, when MLAs were assigned to the booth campaign, he played an active role as well. 'Technically, I am a Nishad Party MLA' Rishi Tripathi says, ‘Technically, I am a Nishad Party MLA. I have been a General Secretary in the BJP organization. Amit Shah is the Home Minister of the country. The BJP and the Nishad Party are alliance partners. Nishad Party workers had come to meet me regarding the reservation issue. I definitely attend any meeting or program information I receive from the BJP-Nishad Party.’ Nishad Party MLA Vivekanand Pandey is also a person who came from the BJP organization. His Facebook page cover features a picture of him taken with PM Modi. Meanwhile, in his profile picture, he is seen with CM Yogi. However, both the BJP and Nishad Party flags are displayed on his vehicle. 'Both parties in the alliance are like elder and younger brothers' Vivekananda Pandey told Dainik Bhaskar, ''Both parties in the alliance are like elder and younger brothers. I recently attended the party's foundation day. I participate in every event of both parties. I am a person associated with the BJP organization, but I was elected as an MLA from the Nishad Party. For me, the leaders of both parties are worthy of respect.'' Nishad Party MLA Ramesh Singh is currently the leader of the legislative party. His father, Kunwar Haribansh Singh, has been an MP from Pratapgarh Lok Sabha constituency representing Apna Dal (S). Ramesh Singh's Facebook page cover features pictures of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, BJP National General Secretary Nitin Nabin, UP BJP President Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and both Deputy Chief Ministers Brajesh Pathak and Keshav Prasad Maurya. Ramesh Singh is also seen with CM Yogi in his profile picture. 'I keep meeting the CM for development works' MLA Ramesh Singh said, 'The Nishad Party flag is on my car. I will continue to contest elections from the Nishad Party in the future as well. Yogi Adityanath is our CM. We are an ally of the government. Due to development works in the region, I often meet the CM. We provide full support-physically, mentally, and financially-to every conference and program of our party.' Only one MLA who left BJP, stays honestly with the Nishad Party Vipul Dubey, the MLA from the Gyanpur seat of Bhadohi (Sant Ravidas Nagar) district, also left the BJP and joined the Nishad Party before the 2022 elections. He entered active politics in 2015 by winning the Gram Pradhan election. In 2021, he lost the District Panchayat member election. Then, the Nishad Party denied a ticket to its incumbent MLA Vijay Mishra and fielded him instead, and he won. Vipul Dubey has put up a picture of himself with workers wearing Nishad Party caps on the cover of his Facebook page. In his profile picture, he is alone.

stories.title: SP may contest 328 seats in UP polls:Preparing to give 75 seats to Congress; SP candidates may contest some of them
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) may field candidates on 328 seats in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, while 75 seats are being considered for the Congress. However, the Congress is claiming a larger share, seeking to contest around 200 seats. In this situation, what will be the middle ground? Both parties have remained silent on this so far. SP sources say the proposal to give 75 seats to the Congress is under consideration. However, on several of these seats, the Congress could contest under its own symbol while the candidates may be from the SP. Akhilesh Yadav has already hinted at such an arrangement. There is a reason behind this strategy. The Congress still lacks a strong organisational base on the ground in UP, while the state has remained the centre of the SP's politics. The SP recently demonstrated the strength of its organisation during the SIR exercise. Rahul was at the centre in Lok Sabha polls, Akhilesh will lead the Assembly campaign. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Ram Gopal Yadav led the SP's side in the coordination committee, with Udaiveer Singh also playing an important role. Asked how many seats each party would contest in the Assembly elections, Udaiveer said the final decision would be taken by the respective high commands. "Which party will get how many seats in UP will be decided by the high command. Senior leaders continue to meet at the party level and at their residences. The situation during the Lok Sabha elections was completely different from that of the Assembly elections. Rahul Gandhi was kept at the centre of the Lok Sabha campaign. The 2027 election will be fought with Akhilesh Yadav at the centre," he said. On the Congress getting 106 seats in the 2017 Assembly elections, Udaiveer said, "That is history. Circumstances do not remain the same." Congress co-in-charge for UP, Shyam Kumar Daulat, said the alliance in UP was certain, but the final decision on seat-sharing would be taken by Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi. "Both the SP and Congress should have faith in the central leadership," he said. So, understand how the math of 75 seats was calculated SP organization officials say - Congress was given 17 seats in the Lok Sabha elections. One Lok Sabha constituency consists of 5 assembly seats. By this formula, Congress could get 85 seats. According to simple math, 1 assembly seat can be given in every district. But there is a catch here. There are many districts where Congress has no base at all. For example, Mainpuri, Etah, Etawah, Farrukhabad, Firozabad, Azamgarh, Ghazipur, Mau, Rampur, and Moradabad. In such a situation, on what basis will seats be given to them in these districts? In such cases, it could be managed by giving Congress more than one seat in certain other districts. According to the SP's formula, some of the potential seats that may go to Congress could be as follows- Congress may also get seats where SP has not been particularly successful. These could include seats in Western UP like Noida, Hapur, Ghaziabad, Bulandshahr, Mathura, and Agra. The BJP has held these for a long time. Additionally, due to the influence of State President Ajay Rai, seats around Varanasi may also go to Congress. These include Rohaniya, Varanasi North, South, Cantt, and Sevapuri. The final talks on seats are to be held in September. Prior to this, the INDIA bloc meeting was held in Delhi on 8 June. At that time, it was decided to hold a meeting once every two months. According to this, the meeting was supposed to take place in August. However, due to the Parliament session and disruptions in the month of August, this meeting could not be held. SP has finalized 150 candidates so far. This includes 100 names who won in the 2022 assembly elections. 45 new faces are included. The official list is yet to be released. 3 reasons are being cited for giving fewer seats to Congress- 1- SP does not want to repeat the mistake of 2017 In the 2017 elections, there was an alliance between SP and Congress. Congress was allocated 105 seats. However, there were 9 seats where, due to the breakdown of the alliance, candidates from both SP and Congress contested against each other. In this way, Congress contested a total of 114 seats. Meanwhile, SP contested 311 seats. Congress could only win 7 seats. 2- SP itself wants Dalit-Adivasi candidates on 100 seats under the PDA factor SP is entering the election with the PDA factor. It wants to field Dalit and Adivasi candidates on about 100 seats itself. These will be separate from the reserved seats. This is also why SP is preparing to contest more seats. 3- Losses due to delays in Bihar The Mahagathbandhan suffered a major loss in Bihar due to delays in seat sharing and contesting seats where Congress had a weak hold. SP wants to avoid this mistake in UP and make decisions in time. SP wants to give Congress only those seats, and only as many, where it has real strength, so that the victory of the alliance can be ensured. Why is Congress forced to accept SP's conditions? In the 2022 assembly elections, Congress got only 2 seats by fighting alone. The 6 seats won in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections were possible only because of the alliance with SP. The Congress leadership will not take the risk of losing like in 2022 by fighting alone, so it will have to agree to SP's conditions. Even if the state unit opposes it, the final decision will be taken by Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav only. At the same time, SP also needs Congress's support to prevent the fragmentation of Muslim voters and to avoid a direct contest.

stories.title: Singer’s wife says, ‘Yogi ji answered in his own style’:After 2 shooters killed in encounter, she says others should meet the same fate too
stories.summary: “The process of getting justice has begun. We have received some relief. CM Yogi ji has responded in his own style and shown what he can do. This is why he is considered so strict on law and order. He took this case very seriously. But the job is not over yet. It will be complete only when everyone involved in this case meets the same fate.” Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan’s wife Seema told Dainik Bhaskar this after shooters Sumit and Mohit were killed in an encounter. His sister Reena said, “The deaths of two accused have brought some satisfaction. But we will not be fully satisfied until those behind the entire case are eliminated.” On Monday morning, Shamli police killed the singer’s two alleged shooters, Sumit (24) and Mohit (22), in an encounter. Before the encounter, Seema had said that she would set herself on fire if her husband did not get justice. She had said officials had asked for two days’ time, but no arrests had been made. According to her, they had only given assurances, and the police response appeared sluggish. Read the singer’s wife’s first interview after the encounter Question: Did you not trust the police earlier, when you said you would protest outside CM’s residence? Answer: Twenty rounds were fired in the middle of the city. There must have been, or should have been, police around the area. Despite this, so many shots were fired in broad daylight. So, it was natural to raise questions about the law and order situation. Question: At that time, were there also suspicions about some police personnel? Answer: There was no suspicion that police personnel were involved in the murder. However, they did not handle the case properly. Later, though, the police did a good job. The action has now started on a positive note. Question: It is being said that the shooters were tracking Ankit’s location by installing GPS device in his car? Answer: We come from a rural background and do not know much about things like GPS. If someone installs a GPS device in a car, how would we know? If we had even the slightest hint, we would not have allowed Ankit to go to the gym alone. We would have asked for security or done something else. Neither Ankit nor we had any idea that someone was after his life. Question: Do you also need security? Answer: I feel a little unsafe. We have lost a member of our family. All our faces have also become public. We are afraid that something might happen to us too. But we trust the police administration and CM Yogi ji. We hope that we will remain safe under their protection. Sister says, ‘There was negligence by the police and administration too’ Ankit’s sister Reena said, “What can a sister say after losing her brother? If the criminals’ surveillance had been detected earlier, Ankit’s life could have been saved. There was negligence by the police and administration too. If barricading had been put in place immediately after the incident, the criminals could have been stopped from escaping.” Now, see what the wife says further; Seema said Ankit had dedicated his entire life to sports. He started playing kabaddi at the age of 12–13, and by the age of 17–18, he had represented Delhi at district, state and national levels. He suffered a serious spinal cord injury, with a completely displaced disc, and underwent major surgery. Doctors advised him not to continue playing sports. He then started a business but was unsuccessful. Later, he moved into modelling, where he also faced many struggles. “We started this work together. We would plan everything together, which song to do, how it should be prepared, what the music should sound like and how the video should be made,” Seema said. The couple selected songs together and then got the videos made. They did not have enough money to release a song every month. It took them nearly two to three months to produce one song. Seema invested her own money in the work and also suffered significant losses. Ankit gave several hit songs to the Haryanvi music industry and worked very hard, but he never reached the position he had hoped for. According to Seema, nepotism is widespread in the industry. Seema and Ankit met during kabaddi coaching. Seema’s brother was Ankit’s coach. ‘If Ankit had received any threat, he would definitely have told me’ Ankit’s wife Seema denied any old dispute or threat. She said, “If Ankit had received any kind of threat, he would definitely have told me. We shared everything. I also spoke to Ankit at the gym on the day he was killed. We initially talked about family matters. After that, Ankit told me about his new project. He was discussing a new project with Haryanvi singer Amit Saini Rohtakiya. During the conversation, Ankit said he would call me again in around 10 minutes. After that, the incident happened.” Focused on fitness for 12 years, had not eaten bread for 6 years Ankit had been involved in sports since childhood, so he was very conscious about his health and fitness. For the past 10-12 years, he had devoted himself completely to fitness. His diet was not a normal one; rather, he followed a diet designed for building his body. Ankit had not eaten even roti for the past 5-6 years. He ate rice, salad, and lentils in the afternoon. In the morning, he ate oats. In the evening, he had a light meal or fruit. He followed a fixed diet schedule, eating 5-6 times a day. Ankit had prepared himself to a very high level. No model in Haryana had fitness like his. ‘My brother was a kabaddi coach, and that’s how Ankit and I got together’ My relationship with Ankit came through my brother. My brother was Ankit’s kabaddi coach. We met through him and later got married. What I liked most about Ankit was his dedication. After our marriage, I stood by him in everything he did. I had secured my own job before getting married. I have been working as a government teacher in Delhi since 2019, while we got married in 2020. Preparing to contest district panchayat elections, dreamed of building stadium in his village Ankit did not want to limit himself to just singing and modelling. He was preparing to contest the district panchayat elections. His dream was to have a stadium built in his area so that local children could get opportunities to advance. He wanted children from the area to reach the Olympics and the Asian Games. Ankit wanted to do a great deal for the youth. Not even a single singer from the Haryanvi industry reached out Not a single singer, writer, lyricist, or model from the Haryanvi industry contacted our family. No one even came to ask about the family's well-being. I am shocked to see this attitude of the industry. The industry that stands up for artists in songs and makes grand claims did not stand by the family after the murder of one of its own artists. If Ankit had been a Haryanvi artist, perhaps the industry would have rallied around him. But that did not happen in the case of an artist from Uttar Pradesh. My last wish is for a stadium to be built in Ankit's name Seema said, "My husband struggled continuously from childhood until the age of 28-29. He struggled with society and with his health, but despite this, he kept trying to do something good." He wanted to influence young people through fitness so that they would stay healthy. According to him, he did not receive the necessary help or results from the film industry or elsewhere, but he never stopped trying. It is my wish that a stadium be built in this area in Ankit's name so that his memory lives on. Having some means of remembering him would certainly be a good thing. This stadium would not only commemorate Ankit but also keep his dream alive.

stories.summary: West Coyote Hills, a 510-acre former oil field in Fullerton, California, has faced development pressure for five decades. After 25 years of efforts to preserve the land, a plan is now close to completion. California has approved a $95 million purchase of the remaining site, with $75 million already committed. Supporters are seeking the final $20 million to permanently protect the habitat as parkland and a nature preserve.

stories.title: Joseph Martinek bought a Texas farm in 1911; 115 years later, family protects 470 acres
stories.summary: Joseph Martinek purchased a Texas farm in 1911, beginning a family legacy that has lasted 115 years. In 2026, his descendants permanently protected 470 acres outside La Grange through a donated conservation easement. The property preserves farmland, wildlife habitat, open space, water resources and archaeological history while allowing the family to retain ownership and continue stewardship.

stories.title: Chinese man studying in Canada arrested by US for espionage-like activities, sister says 'If my brother is a Chinese spy, then I am Trump's father'
In 1978, New York advocates sought affordable homes; nearly 50 years later, 145-home community is complete
stories.summary: After more than four decades of hurdles, a housing initiative from Long Island, initiated in 1978, has finally come to fruition with 145 affordable homes at Matinecock Court. This $98 million project overcame extensive legal and political challenges since its inception, which is linked to a pivotal Fair Housing Act case that reached the Supreme Court.

Jaishankar says India in touch with Russia, Ukraine to help end war
stories.summary: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is actively engaging with both Ukraine and Russia. He is exploring potential ideas and suggestions to help end the ongoing conflict. India believes dialogue and diplomacy are essential for resolving the protracted war. Minister Jaishankar met with Ukrainian leadership and Polish officials during his visit. Discussions also covered trade, technology, and security cooperation between India and Poland.

stories.title: In 2002, South Australia sank ex-HMAS Hobart in under 3 minutes; 18 years later...
stories.summary: Having been decommissioned and sunk in 2002, the ex-HMAS Hobart has evolved into a lively underwater ecosystem. This former Australian warship is now home to more than fifty distinct fish species, while its submerged structure nurtures an array of filter-feeding organisms. Located in a safeguarded marine park sanctuary, it offers an enticing destination for divers eager to explore successful efforts in habitat rehabilitation.

stories.title: Billionaire heiress Isabel Getty, great-granddaughter of J. Paul Getty, marries Faris McKinnon
stories.summary: Billionaire dynasty heiress Isabel Getty, great-granddaughter of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, has married British financier Faris McKinnon in an intimate London ceremony. The couple exchanged vows at Chelsea Old Town Hall before celebrating at Harry’s Bar in Mayfair. Isabel and Faris later made a stylish exit in a vintage black Rolls-Royce, accompanied by their young son Viggo.

stories.title: Australia’s endangered eastern quolls welcome new joeys; after vanishing from mainland for 60 years
stories.summary: Australia’s endangered eastern quolls are showing signs of recovery after conservationists successfully bred captive-raised animals in Tasmania. One released female has six joeys in her pouch, offering hope for the species’ future. Eastern quolls disappeared from mainland Australia by the 1960s, largely due to habitat loss, disease, road accidents and predation.

stories.title: 'No one could erase Sanatan Dharma': Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath celebrates Janmashtami in Mathura
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said, "The proclamations made by Lord Krishna over 5000 years ago remain just as relevant today. Its relevance is upheld by the principle of 'Paritranaya Sadhunam Vinashaya cha Dushkritam'; wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances."

stories.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami transfers Rs 147 crore pension instalment to over 9.91 lakh beneficiaries
stories.summary: A total of Rs 147.05 crore was transferred directly into the bank accounts of 991,914 beneficiaries. In August, pensions of 5,605 new beneficiaries were also sanctioned under various pension schemes.

stories.title: ‘Developed countries must take lead': India calls for climate finance after Nepal flood
stories.summary: India urged developed nations to lead emissions cuts and aid developing countries. Developed nations must provide finance and technology transfer for climate action. India expressed solidarity and support for Nepal's reconstruction efforts after floods. Nepal clarified no compensation was sought from India or other major economies. Both nations agreed to collaborate on Himalayan climate change impacts.

Ricky Hatton’s mansion, where he was found dead in 2025, sold for £1.5m, £350k below asking price
stories.summary: Late boxing legend Ricky Hatton’s luxury mansion in Greater Manchester has sold for £1.5 million, £350,000 below its original asking price. The five-bedroom property, where Hatton was found dead in 2025, featured a heated indoor pool, jacuzzi, gym, cinema, games room and Manchester City memorabilia. The sale comes amid reports over his estate.

stories.title: Game on, history off: White House unveils MAGA arcade
stories.summary: The White House launched retro-style video games to promote President Trump's agenda. Two immigration games, 'Build the Wall' and 'Rio Run,' sparked significant controversy. Critics argue these games trivialize serious immigration issues and dehumanize migrants. Supporters believe the administration is communicating policy in an accessible language for younger Americans. This initiative reflects a broader effort to reshape America's historical narrative.

In 1972, Illinois used 246,000 cubic yards of coal fly ash beneath 7,500 feet of expressway
stories.summary: In 1972, a groundbreaking Illinois expressway project utilized coal fly ash for highway embankment fill, showcasing remarkable structural integrity over time. Vigilant monitoring revealed no concerns with settlement, frost heave, or groundwater. This successful initiative not only prompted other states to adopt fly ash recycling standards but also demonstrated that industrial byproducts can effectively substitute natural aggregates in construction endeavors.

Bargaining tactics? Why BJP's 'solo pitch' in Punjab may have message for Akalis
stories.summary: In a bold move, the BJP is hinting at a solo run for each of the 117 assembly seats in Punjab. Party leaders have made it clear they'll compete independently. Conversely, Shiromani Akali Dal officials are pushing to renew their partnership with the BJP. Currently, the BJP appears to have the upper hand in negotiations, although both factions remain open to the possibility of joining forces down the line.

stories.title: In 1969, Malcolm Forbes bought Colorado's Trinchera Ranch; 35 years later his family...
stories.summary: The Forbes family has made a significant contribution to conservation by donating an 80,000-acre easement, safeguarding alpine wilderness in southern Colorado from future commercial development. This groundbreaking agreement marks the largest donation of its kind in Colorado's history, establishing permanent restrictions against subdivision and commercial ventures on the historic Trinchera Ranch. It symbolizes 35 years of dedicated stewardship by the Forbes family towards preserving nature.

stories.title: JD Vance reveals his weight loss secret, stunned that VP gets this question at an official press conference but Fox News host has a prediction
'We will formulate plan': Ram Temple's first CEO Jeetendra Mishra after Ayodhya trip
stories.summary: Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra (retd) has assumed charge as the first CEO of the Ram temple trust. He expressed that the responsibility for the Ram temple now rests upon his shoulders. Mishra's appointment follows an administrative overhaul within the trust after donation controversies. He is focused on understanding the temple and trust's operational functions. The trust aims to strengthen administrative and financial systems as temple operations expand.

Mariners raised an American flag after clinching their division days after 9/11; 25 years later...
stories.summary: In a celebration of unity and triumph, a new bronze statue honors a pivotal moment in Seattle Mariners history. It features two former players hoisting the American flag, capturing the spirit of their victorious 2001 division title. This monument is situated in a modern plaza that includes interactive components and fundraising initiatives, with proceeds dedicated to restoring youth baseball and softball fields across Washington state.

stories.title: 'Thank you, dear PM Modi': Meloni signals deepening India-Italy strategic embrace
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his congratulatory message, saying the relationship between Italy and India is “stronger than ever” and highlighting their Special Strategic Partnership. Meloni has served as Italy’s PM since October 22, 2022. On Thursday, after completing 1,413 consecutive days in office, she became the country’s longest continuously serving prime minister since World War II.

‘No free cake’: Vancouver bakery owner calls out NBA star’s family over collaboration request, asks how an NBA legend can't afford a birthday cake for his kid
"You guys were the issue": FaZe Banks drops explosive truth about FaZe Clan’s end
stories.summary: During a recent livestream, FaZe Banks candidly discussed the challenges facing FaZe Clan, pinpointing former members like Stable Ronaldo as key contributors to its decline. He revealed an astonishing eleven million dollar investment in creators that yielded no profits, questioning Ronaldo's financial outcomes pre- and post-FaZe membership. These remarks shed light on underlying tensions and disagreements within the organization.

This vacant California lot is now a refuge from heat waves
stories.summary: In San Ysidro, California, the newly opened La Semilla Community Resiliency Center stands as a vital resource for local residents confronting climate adversity. This innovative center provides essential cooling during sweltering heat and electricity during power failures. Furthermore, it focuses on educating the community about disaster preparedness and sustainable practices, directly tackling critical environmental problems such as pollution and extreme weather conditions.

stories.title: Fire-damaged 1867 Michigan school reborn as a $175,000 public park
Baltimore shopping centre rebounds as 200 community investors take ownership, with 10 new leases and 100+ jobs
stories.summary: Edmondson Village Shopping Center is undergoing a significant transformation driven by local residents. Two hundred community investors now hold a direct ownership stake in the property. Ten new leases have been signed, bringing essential services to the neighborhood. A planned headquarters for Meals on Wheels will create over one hundred jobs. This community ownership model connects residents to the property's economic revival.

stories.title: Meet Kiran Reddy, 18-year-old Georgia teen who became the first Indian American to win Miss Teen USA
stories.summary: Kiran Reddy has made an outstanding mark as the first Indian American crowned Miss Teen USA. Having previously claimed the Miss Georgia Teen USA title, she is celebrated as Georgia's first national winner. A dedicated pre-medical student, Reddy aspires to inspire young girls. She is set to represent the United States at the Miss Teen Universe contest, alongside continuing her academic journey.

Streamer MoistCr1TiKaL drops first look at Godslap animated movie coming in 2028
stories.summary: MoistCr1TiKaL has just announced the Godslap animated movie, a captivating adaptation of his graphic novel. This exciting hand-drawn 2D animation project is produced by Lyrical Animation and Meatier Productions, with animation expertly crafted by Powerhouse Animation Studios, famous for their work on Castlevania. Set in a cyberpunk universe, the plot centers around a young hero taking on a formidable corporation. Production is already underway, targeting a 2028 release.

stories.title: Oakland woman lost $12,145 after scammers posed as Charles Schwab security
stories.summary: An Oakland woman says scammers posing as Charles Schwab security drained her entire $12,145 investment account after a frantic phone call. She denies sharing any information, while Schwab said its investigation found that a verification code was provided to a third party. She is now taking the case to arbitration and has contacted police and the FBI.

How a stranger's advice helped Tiffany Haddish go from living in her car to bying 17 properties
stories.summary: Tiffany Haddish went from experiencing homelessness and living on a $500-a-month budget to building a real estate portfolio of about 17 properties. She credits advice from an accountant she met during a trip to China and Japan for changing her approach to money. She also used acting pay cheques to buy and pay off property.

Former Ravens coach John Harbaugh's 1905 Maryland stone mansion sells for $6M
stories.summary: Former Baltimore Ravens coach John Harbaugh has sold his historic stone mansion in Owings Mills, Maryland, for $6 million. He bought the 9-acre property for $3 million in 2013. Built in 1905, the 9,100-square-foot home has five bedrooms, a carriage house, four-car garage, pool, hot tub and multiple outdoor spaces.

Rahul Gandhi vs C Joseph Vijay: Can TVK chief do what Arvind Kejriwal could not?
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's chief minister Vijay faces a political challenge regarding national leadership. His party, TVK, and the Congress coalition are debating the 2029 prime ministerial candidate. Vijay's rise disrupts traditional state politics and sparks national aspirations. He must balance state leadership with a broader political project. This dynamic creates tension within the ruling coalition. Is he ready to have a direct contest with Rahul Gandhi?

stories.title: Three women survived a deadly Grand Canyon flood after clinging to a rock ledge for 5 hours
stories.summary: Three women survived a dangerous flash flood in the Grand Canyon. They clung to a rock ledge for five hours while debris swept past. Separated briefly, each feared the others had been lost to the waters. A rescue helicopter eventually spotted the stranded hikers and brought them to safety. This survival occurred during a larger disaster which claimed other lives.

stories.title: Russian strike damages WHO warehouse in Ukraine; second such attack in weeks
The story of Tsutomu Yamaguchi, the only survivor of both Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings
stories.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi's remarkable story is one of survival against unimaginable odds, as he endured the horrors of two atomic bombings just days apart in August 1945. Initially in Hiroshima on August 6, he found himself in Nagasaki on August 9. Post-war, Yamaguchi channeled his experiences into activism, passionately advocating for nuclear disarmament at the United Nations, illustrating the catastrophic effects of nuclear armament.

stories.title: A giant 10-sided wave is emerging around Saturn’s south pole, Hubble observations show
stories.summary: Saturn's south pole reveals a giant, evolving 10-sided atmospheric wave. Hubble telescope observations trace subtle signs of this pattern back to 2023. This newly identified feature is embedded in a powerful jet stream and extends through multiple atmospheric layers. Scientists have searched for a southern counterpart to the northern hexagon for decades. This discovery offers a rare chance to observe a major atmospheric pattern developing in real time.

stories.title: A $5.5M Portland power project could remove 400 trees from Forest Park while powering over 55,000 homes; the deal has split conservation groups
stories.summary: Amidst rising concerns, Portland General Electric's tree-removal project has drawn fervent opposition from conservationists who fear for the health of mature forests and wildlife. While the utility argues that this initiative is crucial for ensuring consistent power to households, the city is in the process of evaluating a new application and awaiting feedback from the staff. The decision will ultimately balance environmental impacts with the necessity of electrical reliability.

stories.title: Tech entrepreneur's Martha's Vineyard estate bought for $19 million sells for record $43 million
stories.summary: A 31.59-acre estate in Edgartown on Martha’s Vineyard has sold for a record $43 million. Tech entrepreneur Michael Bronner spent $19.125 million between 2019 and 2023 assembling the property, which includes an 8,994-square-foot, 12-bedroom home. The sale surpassed both the island’s previous $37.5 million record and Massachusetts’ $38.1 million record.

stories.title: Indian-origin London cop Prakash Patel charged with 5 counts of sexual assault
stories.summary: A detective sergeant in London has been charged with five sexual assault offenses involving four women he is familiar with. Following his arrest last April, he was suspended from his position. The Crown Prosecution Service has authorized these charges after a thorough investigation carried out by the Metropolitan Police's professional standards teams.

Following the incident, the pilot-in-command tested non-negative for psycho-active substances. Passengers sustained injuries, and the aircraft suffered considerable cabin damage. After evaluating the situation, the crew chose to proceed to Delhi. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau is diligently examining all aspects of this alarming event.

Scientists reveal 7 countries most likely to survive a global collapse by maintaining society and food production
stories.summary: In an intriguing analysis, two studies have spotlighted seven island nations poised to withstand global calamities. New Zealand emerges as the frontrunner, lauded for its geographic isolation and abundant local resources. Australia, on the other hand, shines in nuclear winter scenarios, showcasing its vast food production potential. Both countries, however, grapple with import dependency for vital supplies, indicating distinct variations in their readiness based on various global crisis models.

stories.title: US House passes bill to stop federal funding of universities boycotting Israel
stories.summary: The US House has approved a bill aimed at halting federal support for universities that boycott Israel, marking a significant political shift that now awaits Senate approval. The vote reflected a mostly partisan divide, with some Democrats voicing concerns about free speech implications. Amid escalating protests against Israel's actions in Gaza, supporters assert that the legislation addresses antisemitism, a claim contested by demonstrators who disagree with its intent.

stories.summary: An IndiGo flight had a minor mishap upon landing in Srinagar, coming into contact with a parking stand pole. Fortunately, all passengers and crew deboarded without issue. Authorities have been alerted, and an investigation is currently in progress. The aircraft involved will undergo necessary maintenance and will return to service once it passes all required inspections.

In 2023, Princeton researchers tested radiative cooling, keeping a building 3.9°C cooler
stories.summary: Researchers tested a building's ability to stay cooler than outside air naturally. A special roof released heat towards the sky, while airflow moved air through openings. This passive system kept the test box significantly cooler than the prevailing outdoor temperature. The experiment demonstrated radiative cooling working with thermal mass and temperature-driven ventilation. This approach offers a way to cool buildings without mechanical systems.

stories.title: Use of drugs serious concern, act on it quickly, AAIB to DGCA on AI Phuket-Delhi flight interim report
stories.summary: An Air India flight experienced severe turbulence and multiple hydraulic failures. The pilot-in-command tested positive for a psychoactive substance after the incident. This led to an interim safety recommendation from the AAIB to the DGCA. The aircraft suffered significant cabin damage during the extreme turbulence event. Investigations into the technical causes of the hydraulic failure are still ongoing.

stories.title: South Florida teens use pizza and tech to fight hunger, delivering 25,000 slices to food deprived families
stories.summary: Meet a passionate brother and sister team from South Florida who launched Pizza for a Purpose, an app aimed at alleviating hunger. This unique platform unites generous donors, local pizzerias, and community organizations, leading to the distribution of over 25,000 pizza slices to families. Their philanthropic journey also includes establishing the Dhanam Foundation, which aims to expand their outreach and charitable efforts significantly.

stories.title: Illinois businessman built a giant wind chime to attract visitors, then made 12 Guinness records
stories.summary: Jim Bolin transformed struggling Casey, Illinois, with giant attractions. What began with a record-breaking wind chime grew into 21 oversized objects and 12 Guinness World Records titles, drawing visitors and national attention to the small town.

stories.summary: An unsettling incident occurred when an Air India pilot's post-flight drug test returned a non-negative result for a psychoactive substance. This followed a dramatic altitude drop over Odisha, resulting in injuries to twenty passengers and four crew members. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau has identified this as a serious problem, calling for the Directorate General of Civil Aviation to respond urgently.

stories.summary: The Hopewell Museum is embarking on a remarkable restoration project for its historic house. Careful attention is being given to preserve original elements such as the floors and windows while integrating modern systems to enhance protection of the museum's collections. This comprehensive renovation aims to ensure the building is well-prepared for future use, with a reopening slated for late 2026.

stories.title: 'Profound inspiration for selfless action': PM Modi extends greetings to nation on Janmashtami
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi shared heartfelt Janmashtami greetings with the nation, reflecting on how Lord Krishna's teachings spur selfless deeds and lead humanity towards a brighter future. President Draupadi Murmu echoed these sentiments, urging all Indians to embody Krishna's virtues. In support, Home Affairs Minister Amit Shah hailed Krishna as the symbol of righteousness, while opposition leader Mallikarjun Kharge extended wishes for joy, harmony, and abundance to all.

Boyer hopes the farmland remains protected for generations.

stories.summary: Two friends, Jim Willis and John Webb, bought a 225-acre overgrazed ranch in Texas in 2000 that could support little beyond cattle. They gradually restored native prairie, planted 3,000 sand plum trees, added a five-acre wetland and changed grazing practices. The work transformed the property into habitat for bobwhite quail, grassland birds, deer, ducks and other wildlife, while also encouraging nearby landowners to join a larger habitat corridor project.

Meet Nithya Ravuri, California school student whose nonprofit has grown to more than 500 members
stories.summary: A California high school senior founded Sevah Neuro, a global network for neurodivergent children. This organization provides resources and social connections, growing to over 500 members worldwide. Sevah Neuro offers a summer fellowship program with life skills and social activities for children. The student-led initiative also engages in legislative advocacy for greater awareness and resources. Future plans include developing an educational book, a mobile app, and physical learning centers.

stories.title: In 2002, Idaho buried nearly 300 tons of crushed waste glass beneath Highway 75
stories.summary: Idaho's innovative approach has seen nearly 300 tonnes of waste glass repurposed as road foundation material, addressing both engineering challenges and local waste management issues. The crushed glass cullet, strategically laid beneath a highway section, has proven to be an effective solution, showcasing the potential of recycling in constructing sustainable infrastructure. This project represents a significant advancement in civil engineering practices through resource optimization.

Built in 1906 to carry coal, five West Virginia railroad bridges to be restored for hikers
stories.summary: More than a century after five railroad bridges were built in 1906 to carry coal through West Virginia’s New River Gorge, an $11.8 million project is now restoring them for public use. The work will repair the historic Rend Trail, replace ageing wooden bridge structures, improve safety and accessibility, and reconnect the 3.2-mile trail with nearby community routes. The National Park Service expects the project to take about 16 months, with the full trail expected to reopen next fall.

stories.title: Meet Jonathan Thai, the 17-year-old whose nonprofit raised $30,000, donated 400 bikes
stories.summary: After a local retailer slashed community biking programs, a Georgia teenager took action by founding Pedal Forward. This initiative has successfully raised over thirty thousand dollars, providing four hundred bicycles to children in need. Hundreds have benefited from free cycling skills clinics, and the organization's reach is expanding into Tennessee and New York. Now, Pedal Forward is setting its sights internationally, planning humanitarian efforts in Vietnam.

In 2009, Washington removed a century-old dike and let tides reclaim 762 acres
stories.summary: In 2009, the decision to remove sea dikes from the Nisqually River Delta paved the way for a remarkable transformation, rejuvenating 762 acres of marshland. Young Chinook salmon swiftly adapted to the new tidal channels, fostering their feeding and growth. This comprehensive restoration successfully re-established 21 miles of ancestral tidal channels with Puget Sound, showcasing a promising blueprint for coastal resilience in the West Coast regions.

Denims, Kaceytron, Frogan and SeanDaBlack became involved in a copyright dispute surrounding Klein's “Content Nuke: Hasan Piker” video, while iDubbbz faced a separate defamation lawsuit. One case settled, another ended in default, one remains active, and the final lawsuit was dropped after an apology from Jomha.

stories.title: In 2016, conservationists put the bends back into a Lake District river straightened 200 years earlier
stories.summary: Conservationists undertook an inspiring project to restore the natural meanders of Swindale Beck, which had been straightened for centuries. Within just a few months, the restored gravel beds welcomed back the Atlantic salmon to spawn, while also decreasing flood risks and enhancing drinking water quality for millions. This remarkable recovery fostered a thriving habitat for aquatic insects and river birds, ultimately earning the UK River Prize in 2022.

In 2020, Ohio removed a dam from the once-polluted Cuyahoga River; it reopened 39 km of habitat
stories.summary: The removal of the Brecksville Diversion Dam has enhanced river habitats, allowing migrating fish to thrive. Researchers documented the arrival of fifteen new fish species within the lower Cuyahoga River. While native species have successfully reestablished their presence, the advent of nonnative species also marked a significant change in the ecosystem. Ongoing efforts to eliminate more dams aim to further rejuvenate the Cuyahoga River basin for future generations.

stories.title: At 15, Jim Bishop bought 2.5 acres for $450; he spent 50 years building a castle that is world's largest one-man project
stories.summary: For over five decades, Jim Bishop dedicated his life to building the biggest one-man castle in the world, starting in 1969. His ambition was fueled by a determination to silence skeptics, initially using his own funds and later gathering donations. After Jim's passing in November 2024, his son Daniel has taken up the monumental task, ensuring the legacy of this extraordinary masterpiece lives on.

stories.title: In 1967, astronaut Vance Brand bought 160 acres beside Rocky Mountain National Park for $32,000
stories.summary: In a generous act, former astronaut Vance Brand has gifted forty acres of land to Rocky Mountain National Park. This pristine, undeveloped forest area now forms part of the park's eastern boundary, following congressional legislation passed in 2021 to officially recognize the donation. Protecting popular hiking trails from potential development, this land also ensures the preservation of essential high-elevation ecosystems for the enjoyment of future generations.

In 1964, a couple bought 535 acres in North Carolina and built a summer home there; decades later...
stories.summary: Transforming a cherished family haven into a hub for environmental research, this 535-acre property in North Carolina has been generously donated to the National Park Service. Now known as the Appalachian Highlands Science Learning Center, it plays a crucial role in studying the impacts of climate change and preserving the unique biodiversity of high-elevation ecosystems. Ongoing scientific investigations and educational initiatives thrive here, ensuring this legacy benefits future generations.

stories.title: Gloria Steinem dies at 92: Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham pay tribute to feminist icon
stories.summary: Gloria Steinem, the pioneering feminist activist, author and journalist, has passed away at 92. Following her death, Hillary Clinton, Meghan Markle, Lena Dunham and others paid heartfelt tributes, remembering her influence, generosity and lifelong fight for equality. From women’s rights to reproductive freedom, Steinem’s work inspired generations and left an enduring mark on society.

Nepal floods: No bodies to cremate, kin burn kusha effigies as hopes fade for missing
stories.summary: Families in Nuwakot and Rasuwa performed symbolic cremations for missing flood victims. Relatives used kusha grass effigies when bodies could not be recovered. Searches for missing kin proved unsuccessful across various locations. Priests guided families through traditional rituals for liberating souls. Over one hundred effigies were cremated in Kathmandu's Pashupati Aryaghat.

stories.title: A Virginia mountaintop was scarred by coal mining; it now holds a 200,000-square-foot high school
stories.summary: In Buchanan County, Virginia, a state-of-the-art high school has been inaugurated on land reclaimed from mining activities. This new educational facility brings together four outdated schools into a single, modern campus. It provides a variety of academic and vocational options for students while aiming to lessen resource inequalities and promote local youth resilience, showcasing a major commitment to the community's development.

Garnett purchased the Pacific Coast Highway property for $6.4 million in 2003 and began building a custom home that remained unfinished. Following a failed $16 million sale and legal disputes, the estate was completed and transformed into a luxury residence.

stories.title: A dying mother’s wish protects 2,506 acres ranch
stories.summary: David Ellsbury honored his late mother's wish by safeguarding the family's cherished Diamond E Ranch from development. Spanning 2,506 acres, this land is now forever shielded by a land trust, ensuring that future generations can enjoy its unspoiled beauty. The ranching traditions of the family will thrive on this preserved estate.

stories.summary: At least five African migrants died after their boat encountered trouble at sea. Forty-four survivors were rescued and brought to safety near Gran Canaria. Survivors reported being adrift for nearly a month without provisions. Many migrants suffered dehydration and illness after drinking seawater. The Atlantic route to the Canary Islands remains a dangerous journey.

stories.title: Kodak retiree finds new animal in moss from New York log; scientists confirm it as a new tardigrade
stories.summary: A retired Kodak finance worker and longtime volunteer, Judy Dobles, discovered a previously unknown tardigrade species after collecting moss from a log at New York’s Cumming Nature Center and examining it under a microscope. The species was formally recognised about a year later. Named Mesocrista ojagwaji, it adds to the growing list of tardigrades identified in New York and highlights how much microscopic life remains to be studied.

stories.summary: Peatlands, which store significant global soil carbon, are now releasing it. Warming temperatures cause these ecosystems to shift from carbon accumulators to emitters. This transition occurs rapidly, even with modest warming of four degrees Fahrenheit. Researchers observed carbon loss rates significantly faster than historical accumulation rates. These findings impact global climate forecasting models and future predictions.

This incident sheds light on the escalating issue of mail theft and cheque washing in the Bay Area. Authorities note a concerning rise in mail theft incidents from both postal collection and home mailboxes. For seniors relying on cheques, retrieving lost funds can be particularly challenging.

stories.summary: A 431-acre waterfront parcel in Gloucester County has been officially added to Machicomoco State Park. stories.summary: In an ambitious forest restoration initiative in New Hampshire, researchers sought to mitigate the effects of acid rain. They introduced calcium-rich minerals, leading to an initial boost in tree vitality and growth. However, this solution inadvertently resulted in a staggering increase in nitrogen levels in nearby streams, releasing thirty times more inorganic nitrogen compared to untreated regions. This outcome underscores the intricate dynamics of ecosystems in response to human intervention.

The property has direct ocean access through a private tunnel and includes an oceanfront cabana.

stories.title: In 2001, synthetic estrogen was added to an Ontario lake; its minnow population collapsed after 2 seasons
stories.summary: A groundbreaking experiment conducted in Ontario's Lake 260 unveiled alarming ecological consequences stemming from synthetic estrogen exposure. The minuscule amounts of 17α-ethynylestradiol resulted in reproductive failure among fathead minnows, nearly driving the species to extinction. This critical study highlighted how even minimal contaminant levels can dramatically disrupt aquatic ecosystems. Researchers caution that wastewater containing estrogens poses significant threats to aquatic biodiversity.

stories.summary: An earthquake of magnitude five struck Tibet on Thursday. Rescue operations continue following catastrophic flooding near the Gyirong border crossing. Landslides continue to pose a significant concern for rescue teams.

The government blames human trafficking and misinformation for the perilous crossings, though Morocco refutes claims of managing this mass movement.

stories.title: In 2010, US scientists tracked dye 41.2 miles in Montana’s Missouri River; a reservoir held it 8.2 hours
stories.summary: Scientists conducted a dye-tracing experiment on Montana's Missouri River. This study examined how substances move through the waterway over forty miles. The dye traveled at different speeds through various river sections and reservoirs. Researchers measured how the dye plume spread along the river's direction. This data aids in predicting contaminant movement and planning for accidental spills.

stories.title: Retired US nurse loses over $200,000 to scam, then gets $80,000 tax bill and has to sell home

The financial trouble continued when the IRS sent her an $80,000 tax bill on the money she had withdrawn and lost. Unable to pay, she sold her home and moved into a small apartment while continuing to repay the tax debt.

stories.title: Valerie vanished on Kangaroo Island in 2023 and was found alive 529 days later
stories.summary: Valerie, the brave miniature dachshund, made a remarkable return after 529 days lost on Kangaroo Island. Now, she’s navigating the joys and challenges of reuniting with her family after such a lengthy absence.

Stakeholder consultations are underway to finalize the decision on extending this program.

stories.summary: In Pinellas County, a resident dodged a cunning warrant scam that sought thousands of dollars. Fraudsters pretended to be law enforcement officials, delivering counterfeit arrest warrants via email. The victim was coerced into wiring money to evade arrest, but thanks to his wife's phone monitoring, authorities intervened. Residents are encouraged to verify any official demands through legitimate sources to avoid such traps.

Ongoing efforts continue to protect the Grand Canyon's native fish populations.

stories.summary: In an unforeseen event, an IndiGo aircraft flying from Doha to Bengaluru was rerouted to Muscat due to the pilot falling ill en route. Fortunately, the pilot received prompt medical care upon landing and is recovering well. stories.summary: Two Amazon delivery drivers in Covington, Kentucky, helped save the life of an 85-year-old woman who collapsed after they delivered a printer to her home. One driver performed the Heimlich manoeuvre while the other called paramedics, who arrived within five minutes.

The Park Ranch, located near Markleeville, transitioned to Alpine County's management in August, with public access planned following the development of a thorough management strategy.

stories.summary: In July, UK mortgage approvals for home purchases hit a new low, highlighting a weakened demand in the housing market amid rising borrowing costs. The experiment was later ended, the site cleaned up, and radioactive contamination remains underground in the blast zone.

Laboratory tests indicate the vessel likely originated from Roman Africa. Evidence for this cult on the Iberian Peninsula is generally scarce. The find highlights the quiet reach of ancient religious practices into rural areas.

12 artificial reefs created in 1998 boosted local fish numbers and species richness off Miami Beach
stories.summary: A 2002 study examined 12 artificial reefs built off Miami Beach using limestone boulders, concrete-gravel aggregate and concrete mixed with waste tyre chips. Divers surveyed the reefs every two months from October 1998 to February 2001, recording fish species, numbers and sizes, along with spiny lobsters. They counted 97,826 fish from 146 species. The researchers found no significant difference in fish abundance, biomass or species richness between the three reef materials. However, comparisons before and after deployment showed that the artificial reefs increased local fish abundance and species richness.

stories.summary: Clint Eastwood's previous artichoke farm is now being transformed into a significant wetland restoration initiative. This remarkable project aims to bolster flood protection for the surrounding communities. With the Eastwoods' generous donation, the area will see restoration of essential riparian and wetland ecosystems, fostering wildlife and promoting a more resilient river system. This change converts agricultural land into vital open space, enhancing both safety and community health.

stories.title: Residential complex and possible wine press found near Sekhmet Temple at Egypt’s Memphis
stories.summary: An Egyptian-Chinese archaeological mission found a residential complex near Memphis's Temple of Sekhmet. Grape seeds and a limestone structure suggest a possible ancient wine press was present. Inscribed stone blocks and statue fragments also emerged from the excavation site. These findings offer insights into daily life and activities around the temple. The discoveries add significant layers to the archaeological record of ancient Memphis.

stories.title: An Iowa priest vowed to build a shrine if he survived pneumonia; after recovering, he spent 42 years using over 100 train carloads of stone to create it
stories.summary: The Grotto of the Redemption in West Bend, Iowa, owes its existence to a young seminarian's promise made during his illness. Initiated by Father Dobberstein, the monumental structure took an astonishing 42 years to complete. Utilizing a variety of geological elements, over 100 train carloads of stones were involved in its construction, making it a celebrated historic landmark and one of the largest man-made grottos globally.

Satheesan asserted that women must join the mainstream, stating that such views are unsuitable for developing Kerala. Labour Minister Bindu Krishna also criticised the cleric's remarks, calling them regressive for women's rights. Aboobacker defended directives limiting women's presence at religious events, citing Quranic interpretations.

This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

stories.summary: Teeth unearthed in Osaka have unveiled a diverse dietary landscape of commoners, revealing that their dental calculus held traces of proteins from fish, mammals, and plants. stories.title: Texas WWII veteran’s remarkable century is being celebrated with a heartfelt tribute
