stories.title: NASA tests GPS-free navigation using other satellites and space debris as landmarks
stories.summary: NASA has tested FALCON, a system that lets satellites navigate without GPS by using other spacecraft and orbital debris as reference points. During a three-day test, the system autonomously improved the known orbits of more than 200 space objects while also calculating the position of NASA’s Starling spacecraft.

stories.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 750 dead, 20,000 deployed as rising rivers hamper rescue ops
stories.summary: Nepal and Tibet floods have claimed 750 lives and left over 3,000 missing. Rescuers continue operations amid warnings of fresh flooding and difficult conditions. Hundreds are believed trapped in hydropower tunnels, requiring specialized international assistance. India and China are providing crucial support including forensic experts and relief supplies. Infrastructure damage has cut off communities, while aid efforts are ongoing.

stories.title: 1 in 5 food samples fails: Why so few cases end in conviction
NEET-PG 2026 exam at Jaipur centre rescheduled to September 5 over power outage
stories.summary: The NEET-PG 2026 examination at a Jaipur centre was rescheduled for September 5. This decision followed power outages and technical disruptions during the test on Sunday. Nearly 300 candidates were affected by the rescheduling at the Sitapura centre. Aspirants reported repeated computer shutdowns and system failures during the examination. Officials are investigating the technical arrangements and their impact on the exam's fairness.

stories.title: American startup raises $180 million to drill rock over 5km deep to build world's first superhot geothermal plant at 500 °C
stories.summary: Quaise Energy has successfully raised $180 million for its groundbreaking superhot geothermal plant initiative. Utilizing cutting-edge microwave technology, the project vaporizes rock instead of using conventional drill bits. Collaboration with Nabors Industries will provide essential drilling expertise and equipment. The Obsidian Project, located in Oregon, is set to generate 50 MW by 2030, paving the way for a sustainable energy future.

stories.title: A Colombian man struggling to build his own home created Lego-like bricks from recycled plastic
stories.summary: A Colombian architect helped develop Lego-like building blocks made from recycled plastic and rubber to create temporary and permanent homes. The system was used to build shelters for 42 displaced families in Guapi in 2015. Four people could assemble a 40-square-metre house in five days, without using glue, cement or water.

stories.title: USS Abraham Lincoln sails past Singapore on way home after gruelling Middle East deployment
stories.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, an aircraft carrier, is heading back home after more than 250 days of supporting operations in the Middle East, recently passing by Singapore. Despite reports of declining crew morale and supply difficulties, US Navy representatives have rejected the idea of a widespread mental health crisis. The ship is expected to stop in Thailand before concluding its journey back to the US.

stories.title: ‘Identify your real enemy’: Khamenei urges Gulf rulers to unite, defend each other
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader urged Gulf rulers to identify their real enemy and confront it. He also called for Muslim unity and mutual defense against external threats. The message comes amid ongoing war and significant economic pressure on Iran. Iranian President dismissed speculation about the leader's health, stating he is healthy. Diplomacy and defense remain Iran's complementary approach to national interests.

stories.title: 'Drug-free India' to 'vocal for local': Key quotes from PM Modi’s 137th Mann Ki Baat
stories.summary: In the latest episode of Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Modi focused on grassroots movements and national initiatives, emphasizing the role of technology in preserving history alongside the importance of a drug-free India. The contributions of women street vendors and sanitation campaigns were also highlighted. The Prime Minister called for greater support for local products as the festive season approaches, encouraging individuals to transform environmental stewardship into thriving businesses.

stories.title: A 55-year-old Missouri official reached the 13,804-foot summit of Wyoming's highest mountain
stories.summary: In a remarkable tale of survival, a Missouri deputy attorney general was found alive after an arduous five-day ordeal on Gannett Peak. Despite achieving his goal of reaching the summit, he faced severe dehydration and confusion near Scott Lake. Fortunately, search teams successfully located him amidst the challenging terrain, and he is now in recovery, expressing heartfelt gratitude to his rescuers for their relentless efforts.

stories.title: Indian-origin teen accused of killing family allegedly used ChatGPT for ‘fantasy stories’
stories.summary: A tutor's alarming visit in Acton, Massachusetts, unveiled a grim double homicide involving a mother and her young son. The police later apprehended the grieving elder sibling in his mother's car nearby. Disturbingly, prosecutors disclosed that the teenager employed AI and ChatGPT to delve into hypothetical murder scenarios, prompting a critical examination of artificial intelligence's influence on harmful behaviors.

stories.title: Billboard removal row: Abhishek Banerjee receives police notice over office scuffle
stories.summary: Billboard removal row: Abhishek Banerjee receives police notice over office scuffle

stories.title: Several injured after shots fired at event in Switzerland's Aarau
4.9-magnitude earthquake hits Afghanistan near Hindu Kush
Kim Jong UN shakes up North Korea’s military, dismisses defence minister No Kwang Chol
stories.summary: North Korea has shaken up its military hierarchy by removing the defense minister, a move approved by Kim Jong Un in a recent leadership meeting. This change mirrors advancements at the nation's weapons research center, which has introduced new combat weapon systems. As tensions rise, trilateral military drills involving South Korea, the US, and Japan will carry on, designed to counter North Korea's ongoing nuclear and missile provocations.

stories.title: PM Modi received by Uzbek President Mirziyoyev in Tashkent, leaders share car ride
High-level review meet held over proposed 'ARISE' project for coastal projection and climate resilience in Odisha
Fontana, Italian master of colour photography, dies
Risk of lake burst near Nepal disaster site wanes
England’s water network buckles under sudden summer drought
Zimbabwe crash involving church minibus kills 27
US set to take control of major portion of Venezuelan oil wealth
Russia is teaching its children to fight the wars of the future
Trump-Putin-Zelenskyy summit floated in secret Moscow talks: Report
stories.summary: John Ratcliffe, the CIA Director, is advocating for a trilateral summit involving the US, Russia, and Ukraine, with hopes of revitalizing diplomatic negotiations aimed at resolving the ongoing conflict. He recently conferred with Russian intelligence heads to discuss strategies for encouraging President Putin to engage in talks. US officials have updated President Zelenskyy about these ongoing discussions, yet skepticism amongst Ukrainian officials persists regarding Russia's motives amid potential escalations.

stories.title: 'RSS vision is to see the world as one': Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat at New York event
'Slippages reveal design flaw on Kanpur-Lucknow e-way'
stories.summary: Slippages on the Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway suggest design issues, not construction defects. Affected stretches will require rebuilding from the ground up, officials stated. A preliminary investigation identified weak, plastic soil as a primary cause. Poor drainage also contributed to the expressway's structural problems. The government awaits a final report on the detailed investigation.

stories.title: BJP-SAD alliance revival gains ground ahead of Punjab polls
stories.summary: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal may revive their alliance for upcoming Punjab assembly elections. Both parties acknowledge this partnership as their strongest option despite seat-sharing disagreements. Talks have intensified since Prime Minister Narendra Modi met SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal recently. The BJP seeks a larger seat share and greater government role, reflecting its increased vote share.

stories.title: Congress & BJP clash over Haldwani ‘purification’ row, Rahul seeks FIR
stories.summary: BJP and Congress clashed over allegations of rally venue purification. Rahul Gandhi demanded an FIR, linking it to untouchability practices. BJP rebutted charges, showing organizers' videos and questioning the delay. Organizers stated a hawan followed cleaning for Ramlila, denying BJP links. Both parties exchanged accusations regarding caste divisions and past incidents.

stories.title: August rainfall fails to reduce India's monsoon deficit
stories.summary: India's cumulative monsoon rainfall deficit remains despite August's better-than-expected rains. This deficit has caused a significant acreage gap in kharif crop sowing. Paddy and maize acreage have both reported notable declines compared to last year. Erratic rainfall distribution prevented increased acreage for most kharif crops. Several states, including Bihar and Andhra Pradesh, face substantial rainfall deficits.

stories.title: FSSAI bans Everest, LG from selling hing
stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has issued prohibition orders against two spice companies. Everest Food Products and Laljee Godhoo and Company faced these orders for non-compliance issues. Samples of compounded asafoetida and hing powder did not meet alcohol-soluble extract requirements. Earlier reviews also found violations in other masala products from Everest. These actions highlight ongoing food safety scrutiny within the Indian market.

stories.title: Man on Phuket-B’luru flight tries to hide drugs in overhead panel, held
stories.summary: A passenger flying from Phuket to Bengaluru allegedly tried to hide narcotics. He attempted to conceal thirteen packets of contraband substance in an overhead panel. The passenger then discarded some of the substance into the lavatory bin. Upon landing in Bangalore, customs officials arrested the individual at the aerobridge. Air India Express is cooperating with authorities in the ongoing investigation.

stories.title: BJP president pulls up 3 Delhi MPs for visiting Sajjan Kumar’s house
stories.summary: Nitin Nabin, the BJP president, took disciplinary action against three Delhi MPs who visited the recently deceased Sajjan Kumar's home. Kumar, notorious for his conviction in the anti-Sikh riots, passed away at the age of eighty. This controversial visit comes at a crucial time for the party as they prepare for the Punjab assembly elections.

stories.title: Will work with SCO to free region from terror: PM Modi ahead of summit
stories.summary: On his diplomatic mission to Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, Prime Minister Modi aims to bolster India's regional aspirations and forge stronger ties. At the SCO summit, he will advocate for collective efforts against terrorism and initiate dialogue on trade and strategic collaboration. This trip underscores India’s dedication to nurturing historical connections and fostering prosperity for all involved nations.

stories.title: FBI lowers hiring bar: Getting services from prostitutes, stealing from employer, bestiality not automatic deal-breakers
An entrepreneur began melting discarded plastic; within three years his startup had built...
stories.summary: In a remarkable daily effort, workers in Mexico convert plastic waste into robust building panels, driving change for impoverished families. Spearheaded by the social enterprise EcoDom, this eco-friendly solution tackles pressing issues of pollution and inadequate housing. Informal waste collectors benefit significantly from improved purchasing deals, and this sustainable model aims to reach broader audiences worldwide, striving to alleviate waste and poverty challenges.

stories.title: Unfinished for nearly 30 years, Hollywood Video’s founder's Oregon mansion is up for $4.7 million
stories.summary: A nearly 52,000-square-foot mansion in West Linn, Oregon, has remained unfinished for almost 30 years and is now listed for $4.7 million. Hollywood Video founder Mark Wattles bought the 32-acre property for $1.25 million in 1994 and spent about $12 million on the project. Two later owners also had plans for the estate, but the mansion was never completed.

stories.title: In 2020, four engineers started Moment Energy in a British Columbia garage; 6 years later...
stories.summary: Moment Energy has launched its most extensive second-life battery manufacturing plant, transforming used electric vehicle batteries into essential energy storage systems. This innovative facility aims to deliver backup power for various crucial facilities across North America. The company has successfully obtained considerable funding and safety certifications, while also planning to broaden its manufacturing operations into Texas.

Quote of the day by Queen Elizabeth: "But let us not take ourselves too seriously. None of us has a monopoly of…"
'If any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in India, he's not Hindu': RSS' Mohan Bhagwat in US
Haunted Drake’s Island with Grade-II listed house, 6.4-acre site, tunnels goes on sale for over £2M
stories.summary: Drake’s Island, a 6.4-acre historic island in Plymouth Sound, Devon, has gone on sale for offers above £2 million. The former military site features a Grade-II listed Governor’s House, underground tunnels, Tudor fortifications and planning consent for a 43-bed hotel. Fortified in the 16th century, the island also has a mysterious, reportedly haunted past.

stories.title: Pakistan hospital fire: 8 officials suspended over deaths of 14 newborns
'Congress has become issue-less, pushing forward unnecessary issues': CM Dhami amid Uttarakhand purification row
New Jersey preserves former farm beside historic Monmouth battlefield after development plans
England turns old fishing nets into a 16-metre, low-carbon footbridge
No one calls UP 'Bimaru' state anymore: CM Yogi inaugurates Rs 305 cr projects in Deoria, says mafia crushed; encephalitis eradicated
stories.summary: Addressing a programme in Deoria, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 80 development projects worth ₹305 crore, Adityanath said encephalitis was not merely a disease but reflected what he described as the "sick mindset" of previous Samajwadi Party and Congress governments.

stories.title: Americans don't always want to move to coastal cities for tech jobs, leaving families: Indian-origin founder Apoorva Govind explains why companies have to hire H-1Bs
‘No threat to UP from Nepal floods’: State Jal Shakti minister says authorities remain on alert
'We do not want to burden people': Auto, taxi unions oppose CNG hike in Delhi
Haiti gang frees 13 women and children days after raid that killed at least 47 people
stories.summary: A gang in Haiti has freed thirteen hostages, including women and children, following a brutal assault. UNICEF played a crucial role in securing their release from a farming community. This incident in Kenscoff underscores the rampant violence impacting children across Haiti. The region has faced numerous fatalities and displacement due to gang activities, although mass abductions are less frequent and often yield unpredictable results for those abducted.

stories.title: From F1 visa to US citizenship: Indian-origin tech leader says high-skilled Indians have it harder than most but H-1B abuse should 100% stop
'New ways to create conflict': BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi as 'suddhikaran' row intensifies
Union ministers Chirag Paswan, Jitan Ram Manjhi clash over quotas, demand each other's resignation

US mother found not guilty in deaths of 2 children over postpartum psychosis amid Lindsay Clancy case

Nepal floods: MEA says 88 Indians rescued, 287 still missing; forensic teams dispatched
'Soldiers attempted mutiny': Niger's def min after gunfire, blasts rock Niamey
New plan to end employment authorization for some spouses of H-1B visa holders: '600,000+ jobs will open up in next 2-4 weeks'
From 'khana bana leti ho' to 'will our lives fit together?' How India's marriage biodata is evolving
Hurricane Katrina forced New Orleans’ Charity Hospital to close in 2005; now it is being transformed into a $500 million medical research hub
stories.summary: The historic Charity Hospital in New Orleans is set to undergo a remarkable transformation into a cutting-edge medical research facility. Spearheaded by Tulane University, this ambitious $500 million project aims to establish a vibrant biomedical innovation hub, with construction kicking off this fall and projected completion by 2029. This redevelopment not only honors the landmark's legacy but also demonstrates a robust commitment to improving healthcare for the Gulf South community.

stories.title: Virginia farmer helps create 2,500-acre wildlife corridor through conservation
stories.summary: Two innovative farmers in Virginia are taking strides to connect wildlife habitats on their private lands. Their commitment to blending agriculture with biodiversity creates crucial corridors for wildlife, allowing seamless movement between expansive protected areas. Backed by various scientific and conservation programs, their initiative protects about 2,500 acres of important terrain, fostering a sustainable environment for diverse species.

stories.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator fined $65,000 for betting on Trump speeches
'Strikes not just near LoC': Ex-Army chief Naravane details how India changed tactics in Op Sindoor
324-million-year-old insect still had swimming paddles
stories.summary: A remarkable fossil unearthed in Texas sheds light on the evolutionary journey of insects transitioning from aquatic to terrestrial life. This ancient species featured paddle-like limbs designed for swimming and additional legs on its abdomen, indicating a semi-aquatic lifestyle in shallow coastal regions. This find is crucial in understanding the slow, gradual adaptations insects underwent over millions of years in their evolutionary history.

stories.title: 'Religious slogans were raised, people responded': Dhami hits back at Rahul over Kharge 'purification' row
‘Do ministers feed their own children expired food?’ Abhijeet Dipke during ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign
BJP chief Nitin Nabin expresses displeasure over 3 party MPs visiting Sajjan Kumar residence
Evening Newswrap: Nepal’s flood damage nears 10% of economy; drunk man rapes mother in UP's Hathras & more
Burnham differs from Starmer on assisted dying bill, will skip vote to avoid influencing debate
43-acre Virginia farm behind an inclusive riding programme for people with disabilities listed for $8.4 million
stories.summary: Wheatland Equestrian's historic Virginia property is being sold for approximately $8.4 million. This sale will support the Faith and Family Foundation's long-term mission. The organization began in 1999, offering inclusive equestrian opportunities for all riders. It gained national recognition as a USEF Para-Dressage Center of Excellence. The proceeds will ensure continued services for children and adults with disabilities.

stories.title: ‘UP no longer Bimaru state’: CM Yogi says mafia crushed, encephalitis eradicated; Akhilesh flags gaps
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated the state has shed its "Bimaru" image. He highlighted improvements in healthcare, connectivity, and law and order across Uttar Pradesh. Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticized the state's healthcare system. Yadav alleged significant shortages of doctors and paramedical staff in government hospitals. He promised free treatment and medicines for the poor if his party returns to power.

stories.title: Minnesota removed common carp; lake clarity rose nearly 600% afterward
stories.summary: Pickerel Lake, Minnesota, has battled significant water quality and algal bloom problems for decades, primarily due to invasive common carp taking over the shallow waters. After their removal in 2009, the lake underwent a remarkable ecological revival, with water clarity significantly improving and native aquatic plants flourishing once more. This successful restoration highlights the pivotal role of addressing invasive species in revitalizing ecosystems.

stories.title: Viking woman’s clothes preserved by her jewellery for 1,300 years
stories.summary: Danish archaeologists discovered rare Viking textile remains near Varde. Corrosion from jewelry preserved these ancient wool and linen fragments. This discovery offers a rare glimpse into Viking dress from 1,300 years ago. Researchers will analyze the fibers and teeth for more information. Dating the textiles will reveal if ornaments were new or inherited.

stories.title: Aviation pioneer Glenn L. Martin donated over 2,500 acres in 1954, helping create a refuge for migratory birds
stories.summary: A former private hunting preserve now serves as a vital wildlife refuge. This refuge protects tidal marshes and wooded ridges for migratory birds. Established in 1954, it has since expanded significantly in size. The area provides seasonal shelter for waterfowl and nesting grounds for many birds. It also supports mammals, reptiles, and marine species, preserving the bay's natural landscape.

stories.title: 'Not interested right now': Rahul Gandhi on Sonia Gandhi memoir row, cites 'crime' against Kharge
stories.summary: Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi declined to comment on the controversy surrounding his mother Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, "Belonging," saying his focus was on the “crime” against party president Mallikarjun Kharge. The remarks came amid a row over the book’s publication and editorial changes that were reportedly rejected by Sonia Gandhi.

stories.title: 'Gang of dacoits': Yogi Adityanath says Akhilesh must apologise for UP 'loot and extortion'
stories.summary: In a harsh rebuke, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath labeled the Samajwadi Party a 'gang of dacoits' for allegedly plundering the state treasury during its rule. He proudly showcased the advancements in development and security achieved during his leadership, drawing sharp contrasts with the chaos of previous administrations. Adityanath also referenced the tragic encephalitis fatalities linked to earlier governments, emphasizing the need for responsible governance.

stories.title: No surrender, no dissent: How six months of war hardened Iran’s leadership
stories.summary: Iran's leadership has appointed hard-line military and security officials to key positions. These moves signal a resistance to US pressure and a crackdown on domestic dissent. The new appointments come as Iran faces prolonged confrontation and economic pressure. Hardliners are tightening their grip around the new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei. This consolidation aims to maintain unity and prepare for potential unrest and further conflict.

stories.title: 'Will you suspend them for backstabbing Sikhs?' AAP asks BJP over MPs' visit to Sajjan Kumar's home
McDonald's-backed grants unlock $99.1m for conservation across 100,650 US acres
stories.summary: McDonald's and its partners are actively funding conservation easements throughout the United States. With these grants, they will preserve over 100,000 acres of essential grasslands, providing support for ranching communities and a variety of wildlife. The initiative seeks to secure important habitats and migration paths for numerous species while promoting sustainable practices in beef cattle production.

stories.title: ‘Do you feel you are a lord?’ Bombay HC slams FDA, clears reopening of 5 eateries
A wooden relic that survived the sack of Jerusalem's First Temple was unearthed by archaeologists, now they are finding shocking answers
stories.summary: In a remarkable find, archaeologists uncovered ancient wooden beams from the destruction of Jerusalem's First Temple, dating back over 2,600 years to 586 B.C. These preserved sycamore beams, covered in melted plaster, are believed to have supported the roof of an inner courtyard. By analyzing the growth rings, researchers have accurately dated this crucial archaeological evidence, providing an extraordinary link to Jerusalem's rich and ancient history.

stories.title: Scientists find 1.55 million cubic metres of hidden ice beneath Utah mountain
Present tense, future perfect: Zurich Airport sees 'slower ramp-up' in Noida Airport traffic
stories.summary: The ramp-up of traffic at Noida International Airport is lagging behind expectations, primarily due to the withdrawal of a launch airline and the existing Delhi airport operating under capacity. In its opening month, the new airport managed 104 flights and accommodated 25,000 passengers. Connectivity hurdles and strong competition from Delhi present notable challenges. Despite this, Zurich Airport remains optimistic about the Indian aviation sector's long-term growth outlook.

stories.title: Three forgotten kings may change the accepted timeline of ancient Assyria
stories.summary: Research indicates that ancient Assyrian king lists could have neglected to mention several ephemeral rulers. Evidence points to three monarchs who temporarily ascended the throne amid turbulent political times. Their short reigns might have been intentionally omitted from the official historical timeline, raising questions about the accuracy of Assyria's established chronology.

stories.title: 'Suddhikaran another name for untouchability': Rahul Gandhi accuses BJP, RSS of discrimination against Kharge
Scientists spent 100 years discovering animals, reshaping where we see Earth’s biodiversity hotspots
stories.summary: A groundbreaking study has unveiled that taxonomic advancements have reshaped worldwide biodiversity maps over the last century. While reptile and amphibian diversity has markedly changed, bird and mammal distributions have remained mostly unchanged. Australia and Southeast Asia have been identified as key biodiversity hotspots for these groups. Moreover, factors influencing species richness are also shifting, with precipitation emerging as more crucial.

stories.title: They were digging a sewer when they found gold worth $10.4M
stories.summary: While digging trenches for a new sewage system in Belgium, construction workers stumbled upon an astonishing treasure worth over ten million dollars. This remarkable find consisted of various gold bars and coins. Authorities have secured the precious haul in a high-security federal vault, adhering to Belgian regulations that permit rightful owners a five-year window to claim their treasure.

stories.title: Flyer on Phuket-Bengaluru flight 'tries to hide' drugs in lav overhead panel, held on arrival
Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel thanks India for 'generous support and solidarity' after floods
Nagendra resigned to avoid embarrassment to Congress: DK Shivakumar
stories.summary: B Nagendra has submitted his resignation from the Karnataka cabinet. He cited avoiding embarrassment to the Congress party as his reason. Opposition parties had protested his alleged involvement in an Rs 89 crore scam. Nagendra stated he was voluntarily tendering his resignation after being hurt. The final decision on his resignation will be made after consulting the party high command.

stories.title: In 2002, Alabama architecture students stacked 72,000 worn carpet tiles into the walls of a family home
stories.summary: Students at Rural Studio have transformed donated carpet tiles into the innovative Lucy Carpet House, providing a vital home and prayer space for the Harris family. This initiative is part of a broader effort that has resulted in over 200 projects within Hale County, enabling students to gain hands-on experience while tackling the challenges of affordable housing in rural communities.

stories.title: SC to hear plea seeking mandatory disclosure of ethanol content in petrol on Aug 31
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear a petition on August 31 regarding ethanol labelling. The plea seeks mandatory disclosure of ethanol percentages on petrol nozzles. It also requests a public database for vehicle compatibility with ethanol blends. An expert committee will examine E20's real-world impact on vehicles. The court will review policy files supporting the E20 rollout.

stories.title: A former Illinois school is now a $1.35M accessible park with an inclusive playground and splash pad
stories.summary: On August 26, Galesburg proudly unveiled Cooke Park, a fully accessible neighborhood space built on the site of the former Cooke Elementary School. This ambitious $1.352 million project features an inclusive playground and splash pad, showcasing the community's dedication to inclusivity. The ribbon-cutting ceremony was attended by local officials and community leaders, marking a significant partnership between the government and residents.

stories.title: Rakshabandhan in NYC: Zohran Mamdani celebrates with South Asian seniors
stories.summary: During a heartfelt celebration of Rakshabandhan at India Home, NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani emphasized the festival's profound themes of protection, support, and unity. Drawing parallels to the rakhi's significance, he reaffirmed his dedication to ensuring the welfare of all New Yorkers. The mayor commended India Home for nurturing a sense of community and belonging among seniors, encouraging residents to foster these values citywide.

stories.title: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visits Iskcon’s birthplace in New York, joins food distribution drive
stories.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visited the New York Iskcon temple during his US tour. He participated in a food distribution initiative for homeless individuals. Bhagwat spoke about Krishna consciousness and its role in overcoming global conflicts. The visit precedes his address to the Indian diaspora at Madison Square Garden. Iskcon aims to promote shared values amid world polarization and conflicts.

stories.title: No escape for Trump in hush money case as US judge blocks bid to shift federal court
US to establish first space academy, expand "far beyond the Moon"
stories.summary: President Trump has taken a monumental step by signing an order to create America's inaugural space academy, designed to elevate the nation's future leaders in space exploration. In a momentous interaction, he engaged with astronauts on the International Space Station. This initiative follows prior plans for lunar missions and commercial ventures, culminating in the recognition of the Artemis II crew with the prestigious Congressional Space Medal of Honour.

stories.title: PM Modi begins four-day Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit for SCO summit; what's on agenda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi began a four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic. He will hold bilateral talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent. Modi will then attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. This visit aims to strengthen India's strategic partnerships in Central Asia. The summit will bring together leaders from ten member nations.

stories.title: An 11,000-year-old statue of a human riding a leopard was found at Karahantepe
'I still struggle': Landlady recalls Saudi man who brought 9/11 hijackers to her office
Pakistani drone detected in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch, security forces put LoC sector on high alert
stories.summary: Security forces are on high alert after a Pakistani drone was detected near the LoC. Military personnel tracked the unmanned aerial vehicle over the Rajouri sector on Friday evening. This incident follows several other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir recently. Security forces have intensified search operations in forward areas to detect any dropped materials. Border monitoring remains active as authorities await further official updates on the situation.

stories.title: Ancient Greeks wore jewellery forged from meteorite iron, study finds
Maya Higa Reveals Engagement: Streamer shares ‘best surprise of my life’; fans quiz Caleb vs FaZe Adapt
stories.summary: Maya Higa has announced her engagement to her longtime partner Caleb, sharing proposal photos and calling it the “best surprise” of her life. Unlike the popular streamer, Caleb maintains a largely private life and does not appear to be a prominent content creator. Higa previously revealed they met through mutual friends at a bar and had been together for about a year by 2023. Fans briefly mistook Caleb for streamer FaZe Adapt.

stories.title: Flash floods put focus on India's glacial lakes
stories.summary: Nepal's alarming glacial lake outburst flood serves as a wake-up call for India, which is home to about 200 vulnerable glacial lakes in the Himalayas. The GLOF incident in Sikkim resulted in severe damage, highlighting the urgency of proactive measures. In response, the Indian government has launched a National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme focused on thorough assessments, continuous monitoring, effective early warnings, and raising awareness within local communities.

stories.title: Government tightens norms for e-cycles, e-bikes
Junk foods will soon have labels warning of high salt, sugar and fat
stories.summary: Junk foods will soon feature prominent red warning labels on their packaging. These labels will highlight high levels of salt, sugar, and fat content. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has agreed to this new regulation. This move aims to help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions. The phased implementation will allow the industry time to adjust product formulations.

stories.title: Clean energy push unfair on developing nations: CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: Speaking at the Commonwealth Secretariat in London, CJI Kant said, “Countries that are finally industrialising are being asked to move rapidly towards renewable power, and are often made to bear the brunt of criticism when they cannot move fast enough.” “The challenge, therefore, is to reconcile the urgency of the clean energy transition with the principles of fairness and shared responsibility that must underpin it,” the CJI said.

stories.title: Nilekani committee seeks public ideas to fix exams
stories.summary: The panel, headed by Infosys co-founder and technology expert Nandan Nilekani, was announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month amid heightened scrutiny of the examination system following NEET-UG paper leak controversy and youth protests over alleged lapses in the test’s conduct. It will also look at measures to improve accessibility and inclusion, while factoring in student well-being during the examination process.

stories.title: National Testing Agency gets three senior officers amid exam overhaul
stories.summary: IPS officer Ravi Kumar Singh and IAS officer Prasanna Venkatesh V have been appointed directors at NTA, while Amit Samdariya, a 2016-batch Indian Revenue Service (customs and indirect taxes) officer, will join as joint director. The appointments were cleared through separate personnel ministry orders dated August 27. The personnel ministry has directed all three officers to take charge within three weeks.

stories.title: Sonia memoir row deepens, Congress alleges government pressure
stories.summary: Penguin Random House India has made the decision not to publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir, leading to allegations from Congress regarding external pressure to omit references to Modi and China. In response, Penguin emphasized its commitment to editorial integrity and its role in verifying facts. They remain open to publishing the memoir in India, but uncertainties linger surrounding the rights for its release in the country.

stories.title: From Reds to NGOs: RSS weekly expands ‘dimagi Naxal’ label
stories.summary: In an editorial, ‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”. It said, “As the armed rebellion has failed miserably, the dimagi variant has taken charge.” The editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and NGOs formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”.

stories.title: Nepal floods: Spooked by visuals & reports, tourists cancel bookings, tour operators hit
stories.summary: A Darjeeling couple had planned a 15-day trip to Mansarovar via Kerung in Sept. The Rs 4.4-lakh tour package included permits for entering Tibet. They cancelled the trip after watching videos of Kerung being swept away. Kolkata travel agents Anil Punjabi and Anjani Dhanuka had furrowed brows over rising cancellations even as many sought updates on the safety of other Nepal destinations like Kathmandu, Pokhara, Patan and Lumbini.

In 2024, a Minnesota dairy began turning manure from more than 2,000 cows into renewable gas
stories.summary: In Minnesota, a pioneering dairy farm is transforming cow manure into ultra-low-carbon fuel for vehicles. This innovative facility processes thousands of gallons of manure each day, producing biomethane that enters interstate natural gas pipelines. By capturing methane—a significant greenhouse gas—before it escapes into the atmosphere, this project not only aids the environment but also provides a vital income stream for local dairy farmers.

stories.title: Las Vegas Valley converted 250 million sq ft of lawn to save water, saving 203 billion gallons
stories.summary: Las Vegas is making headlines for its initiative to remove grass lawns, which has successfully conserved billions of gallons of water. Nevertheless, this environmental strategy has led to a concerning increase in local summer land-surface temperatures, soaring by around 20 degrees Celsius. As a response, water agencies are now promoting the use of water-efficient landscaping and shade trees, and new guidelines prevent grass installations in residential yards.

Tim Curry bought a $650K LA home in 1993; after his death, the $7.5M property found a buyer
stories.summary: Tim Curry’s historic Los Feliz home has come under offer for $7.5 million, just hours after the actor’s death at 80. Curry bought the 1922-built property for $650,000 in 1993 and spent years restoring its original details. The Spanish-inspired residence was later owned by stars including Robert Pattinson, Jim Parsons and Aaron Paul.

UNCCD concludes COP17 with new drought resilience and land restoration initiatives
stories.summary: The recently concluded UNCCD conference in Mongolia set the stage for enhanced global drought resilience with innovative initiatives. Highlighted was a significant $1.3 billion commitment for land restoration and drought resilience projects. The newly introduced Drought Resilience Index will aid nations in evaluating their strategies, while the Drought Resilience Investment Facility seeks to attract public and private funding for impactful projects, aiming to scale solutions worldwide.

Uttarakhand CM Dhami announces free bus travel, Pink e-Buses for women on Raksha Bandhan
stories.summary: In a significant announcement, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami revealed a series of initiatives aimed at empowering women. Notably, women aged sixty and older will enjoy free travel on Roadways buses. Additionally, ten electric buses in Dehradun are designated as Pink e-Buses for women’s convenience. Moreover, the loan limit for women's self-employment schemes has been raised to Rs 2.

stories.title: A Houston lawyer bought a 15,000-sq-ft mansion listed for $15.5 million just to demolish it
stories.summary: In River Oaks, Houston lawyer Tony Buzbee has bought a mansion primarily for property expansion. Teaming up with Habitat for Humanity, he aims to salvage valuable construction materials, which will provide substantial support—millions of pounds worth—for affordable housing projects. The planned demolition will allow for the development of a larger private garden estate while enhancing his family's legacy through philanthropic efforts.

In 2024, a Colorado county paid $34 million for a 650-acre ranch owned for more than a century
stories.summary: In a momentous conservation victory, a historic ranch in Colorado has been designated as protected wilderness. This expansion secures an impressive 530 acres of public land, which local officials successfully purchased through a record-breaking deal two years prior. After being privately held for more than a century, this acquisition ensures the enduring protection of crucial wildlife habitats and public access to the land.

Texas farmer loses 600 acres to Google data centre, given just 60 days to leave
stories.summary: In rural Texas, expansive tracts of farmland are increasingly being repurposed for technology ventures, primarily data centers by major tech enterprises. This shift is impacting farmers, especially with resource competition over vital necessities like water. Concerns have been raised by state officials regarding the permanent loss of fertile land, highlighting a significant transition in the region's agricultural landscape.

Japan killed 14,000+ bears after record attacks; 6 people died despite cull, 8,800 more targeted
stories.summary: Japan is currently grappling with a significant rise in bear conflicts, with incidents surging alarmingly. Conservationists are voicing urgent concerns regarding the extensive culling of endangered bear populations. Factors such as extreme heat and declining food sources are pushing bears into human territories in search of food. While the government’s response aims at curtailing bear numbers, critics label this approach as ineffective.
